bills.public_summary: Strengthens legal protections for gender-affirming health care, shielding patients and providers from outside legal action.
bills.last_action: The committee(s) on HHS/CPN has scheduled a public hearing on 03-20-26 9:30AM; Conference Room 229 & Videoconference.

bills.title: RELATING TO MENTAL HEALTH.
bills.description: Amends the existing prohibition on conversion therapy by prohibiting the practice on persons under the age of twenty-five and the advertisement of such practice.  Explicitly provides that talk therapy in the form of pure speech is exempt from the prohibition on conversion therapy.  Takes effect upon the certification by the Attorney General that the Supreme Court of the United States has overturned the holding in Chiles v. Salazar, 116 F.4th 1178 (10th Cir. 2024).  Effective 7/1/3000.  (HD1)
bills.public_summary: Extends the conversion therapy ban to people under 25 and bans advertising it.
bills.last_action: Passed Second Reading as amended in HD 1 and referred to the committee(s) on JHA with Representative(s) Alcos, Garcia, Gedeon, Matsumoto voting aye with reservations; Representative(s) Pierick voting no (1) and Representative(s) Quinlan excused (1).

bills.title: RELATING TO DISCRIMINATION.
bills.description: Prohibits discrimination based on:  (1) The perception that a person possesses certain characteristics; (2) The perception that a person is associated with a person who possesses, or is perceived to possess, certain characteristics; or (3) The intersection or combination of two or more specified characteristics in relation to a person.  (SD1)
bills.public_summary: Expands discrimination protections to cover perceived and intersecting characteristics.
bills.last_action: The committee(s) on JDC has scheduled a public hearing on 03-17-26 9:55AM; Conference Room 016 & Videoconference.

bills.title: RELATING TO PUBLIC TRANSIT.
bills.description: Establishes within the Department of Transportation a subsidized youth transit program for youth who are residents of the State, to be coordinated with the counties.  Authorizes the Department to adopt rules, expand eligibility, and consult with the Department of Education on best practices, under certain conditions.  Establishes the Subsidized Youth Transit Program Special Fund.  Requires biannual evaluations of the new program and Special Fund.  Allocates funds from the Environmental Response, Energy, and Food Security Tax to the Subsidized Youth Transit Program Special Fund.  Appropriates funds into and out of the Subsidized Youth Transit Program Special Fund.  Requires reports to the Legislature.  Effective 7/1/3000.  (HD2)
bills.public_summary: Creates a state-subsidized transit program so Hawaii youth can ride public transportation at little or no cost.
bills.last_action: Reported from HSH (Stand. Com. Rep. No. 528-26) as amended in HD 2, recommending referral to FIN.

bills.title: RELATING TO PESTICIDES.
bills.description: Beginning 1/1/2030, prohibits the use or application of a pesticide containing 1,3-dichloropropene as an active ingredient, such as Telone.  Effective 7/1/3001.  (HD3)
bills.public_summary: Bans use of the pesticide 1,3-dichloropropene, sold as Telone, beginning in 2030.

bills.title: RELATING TO TRANSPORTATION.
bills.description: Authorizes the Department of Transportation to evaluate intersections for the installation of leading pedestrian intervals, accessible pedestrian signals, and other safety improvements, as necessary, at state-owned or operated pedestrian signal heads.  Requires the Department of Transportation, in coordination with the counties, to develop a program that allows pedestrians and community members to request the installation of accessible pedestrian signals at specific intersections.  Effective 7/1/3000.  (HD1)
bills.public_summary: Lets the state add head-start walk signals and accessible crossing signals at state intersections, and lets residents request them.
bills.last_action: Passed Second Reading as amended in HD 1 and referred to the committee(s) on FIN with none voting aye with reservations; none voting no (0) and none excused (0).

bills.title: RELATING TO GOVERNMENT OPERATIONS.
bills.description: Establishes provisions limiting state and federal collaboration for purposes of immigration enforcement operations.  Establishes identification and facial coverings standards for state and federal law enforcement officers.  Establishes criminal offenses for improper facial coverings and lack of visible identification and unauthorized civil immigration arrest or detention.  Effective 7/1/2055.  (SD2)
bills.public_summary: Limits state and county cooperation with federal immigration enforcement and requires officers to be identifiable.
bills.last_action: The committee(s) on PSM/EIG has scheduled a public hearing on 03-23-26 3:00PM; Conference Room 016 & Videoconference.

bills.title: RELATING TO COMMUNITY SCHOOLS.
bills.description: Appropriates funds to the Department of Education to support community schools.  Effective 7/31/2055. (SD1)
bills.public_summary: Funds community schools programs in the Department of Education.

bills.title: RELATING TO HEALTH.
bills.description: Specifies that no person is subject to liability for providing clinical preventive services in accordance with Department of Health recommendations.  Requires health insurers, mutual benefit societies, health maintenance organizations, and plans established by the Hawaii Employer-Union Health Benefits Trust to provide coverage for clinical preventive services.  Authorizes the Department of Health to make recommendations relating to clinical preventive services and issue standing orders for medications and immunizations.  Clarifies that, for coverage for child health supervision services, the prevailing medical standards include recommendations by the Department of Health.  Specifies that coverage for clinical preventive services shall not be denied on the basis of medical necessity or subject to prior authorization.  Specifies that a registered pharmacist may order a vaccine in accordance with the recommendations from the Department of Health.  Exempts this measure from an Auditor impact assessment report.  Effective 1/30/2050.  (SD1)
bills.public_summary: Protects providers who deliver preventive care under state health guidelines and sets insurer coverage requirements for those services.
bills.last_action: The committee(s) on HHS/CPN has scheduled a public hearing on 03-20-26 9:30AM; Conference Room 229 & Videoconference.

bills.title: RELATING TO DECENTRALIZATION OF DEPARTMENT OF EDUCATION FARM TO SCHOOL.
bills.description: Provides that complex area superintendents have the authority to implement the farm to school and farm to school meals programs.  Requires certain school cafeteria supervisors to report directly to complex area superintendents.  Establishes school cafeteria supervisor positions.  Requires the Department of Human Resources Development to conduct a compensation review of school cafeteria supervisor positions.  Appropriates funds.
bills.public_summary: Puts complex area superintendents in charge of farm-to-school meal programs with dedicated cafeteria staff.

bills.title: RELATING TO DEPARTMENT OF EDUCATION FARM TO SCHOOL PROCUREMENT.
bills.description: Requires the Department of Education to establish rules for the procurement of goods and services related to the administration of food programs at public schools that incorporate a geographic preference for unprocessed locally grown and locally raised food products.
bills.public_summary: Requires public school food programs to give purchasing preference to locally grown food.
bills.nickname: Local food preference for school meals

bills.title: RELATING TO RED HILL.
bills.description: Appropriates funds for studies on remediation of substances released from the Red Hill Bulk Fuel Storage Facility; environmental monitoring and testing; research on groundwater modeling and sampling; and independent testing and verification of water data, to be published on a public dashboard.  Requires the Department of Land and Natural Resources to seek reimbursement from the United States Department of Defense.  Effective 11/20/2121.  (SD1)
bills.public_summary: Funds studies, monitoring and independent testing of water affected by the Red Hill fuel leak, published publicly.
bills.last_action: The committee(s) on  PSM recommend(s) that the measure be PASSED, WITH AMENDMENTS.  The votes in PSM were as follows: 3 Aye(s): Senator(s) Fukunaga, Lee, C., Inouye; Aye(s) with reservations: none ; 0 No(es): none; and 2 Excused: Senator(s) Hashimoto, DeCorte.

bills.title: PROPOSING AN AMENDMENT TO ARTICLE I OF THE HAWAII STATE CONSTITUTION TO RECOGNIZE AND PROTECT THE INHERENT AND INALIENABLE RIGHT OF ALL PEOPLE TO CLEAN WATER AND AIR, A HEALTHFUL ENVIRONMENT AND CLIMATE AND HEALTHY NATIVE ECOSYSTEMS AND BEACHES.
bills.description: Proposes a constitutional amendment to ensure that the inherent and inalienable right of the people, including future generations, to clean water and air, a healthful environment and climate and healthy native ecosystems and beaches, shall be protected and shall not be infringed.
bills.public_summary: Proposes a constitutional amendment guaranteeing the right to clean water and air and a healthful climate for future generations.
bills.last_action: Referred to EEP/WAL, JHA, FIN, referral sheet 3

bills.title: RELATING TO THE GREEN FEE.
bills.description: Establishes the Green Fee Transparency and Accountability Program and Green Fee Resiliency Impact Dashboard, to be administered by the Hawaii Climate Change Mitigation and Adaptation Commission.  Appropriates funds.  Effective 7/1/3000.  (SD1)
bills.public_summary: Creates a public dashboard tracking how green fee revenue is spent on climate resilience.

bills.title: RELATING TO HEALTH CARE.
bills.description: Prohibits persons from interfering with another person's access to or from a health care facility or disrupting the normal functioning of a health care facility.  Makes violations a petty misdemeanor.  Establishes a private right of action.  Authorizes the Attorney General to bring an action for injunctive or other equitable relief.  (SD1)
bills.public_summary: Makes blocking access to health care facilities a criminal offense with a private right of action.
bills.last_action: The committee(s) on HHS has scheduled a public hearing on 03-18-26 1:00PM; CR 225 & Videoconference.

bills.title: RELATING TO IMAGE-BASED SEXUAL ABUSE.
bills.description: Establishes the nonconsensual disclosure of intimate or private images as a criminal offense.  Amends the criteria for an extended term of imprisonment to include an offender whose act of attempting to commit or committing the nonconsensual disclosure of intimate images or private images against a minor or vulnerable adult was the proximate cause of the victim's death.  Effective 7/1/3000.  (HD2)
bills.public_summary: Makes nonconsensual disclosure of intimate images a criminal offense with enhanced sentencing.

bills.title: RELATING TO PRIMARY CARE.
bills.description: Establishes the Primary Care Providers Working Group within the State Health Planning and Development Agency to address issues relating to, and develop recommendations for the stabilization of, primary care services in Hawaii.  Requires the Working Group to make a report to the Legislature.  Sunsets the Working Group on 6/30/2027.  Effective 1/1/2050.  (SD1)
bills.public_summary: Creates a working group to recommend ways to stabilize primary care services in Hawaii.
bills.last_action: The committee(s) on HHS has scheduled a public hearing on 03-18-26 1:00PM; CR 225 & Videoconference.

bills.title: RELATING TO THE EMERGENCY MEDICAL SERVICES SPECIAL FUND.
bills.description: Amends the Emergency Medical Services Special Fund by authorizing the deposit of revenues from billable emergency medical services.  Amends the composition and allowable uses of the special fund.  Establishes a cap on the unencumbered and unexpended balance in the special fund.  Exempts expenditures from the special fund from chapters 103D and 103F, HRS.  Discontinues the allocation of cigarette tax revenues to the special fund beginning 1/1/2027.  Effective 7/1/3000.  (SD1)
bills.public_summary: Restructures the emergency medical services fund to accept billing revenue and expand allowed uses.

bills.title: RELATING TO COLORECTAL CANCER.
bills.description: Requires the Department of Human Services to develop and implement a state-funded financial assistance program to offer state-funded colorectal screenings and treatment for certain persons.  Requires state-funded coverage for follow-up treatment for colorectal cancer for certain persons.  Requires coverage to include a follow-up colonoscopy after a positive test result.  Specifies that coverage is not subject to a deductible, copayment, coinsurance, or any other cost-sharing requirements.  Appropriates funds and establishes one full-time equivalent (1.0 FTE) position.  (CD1)
bills.public_summary: Creates a state-funded program covering colorectal cancer screening and treatment for eligible residents.

bills.title: RELATING TO THE UNIVERSITY OF HAWAII CANCER CENTER.
bills.description: Appropriates funds for the University of Hawaii Cancer Center's Hawaii Tumor Registry.  Effective 7/31/2055.  (SD1)
bills.public_summary: Funds the Hawaii Tumor Registry at the University of Hawaii Cancer Center.

bills.title: RELATING TO INSURANCE.
bills.description: Beginning 1/1/2027, requires health insurers, mutual benefit societies, health maintenance organizations, and health plans under the State's Medicaid managed care program to provide coverage for biomarker testing.
bills.public_summary: Requires health plans, including Medicaid managed care, to cover biomarker testing from 2027.
bills.last_action: Referred to HLT/HSH, CPC, FIN, referral sheet 3

bills.title: RELATING TO TAXATION.
bills.description: Establishes a family caregiver tax credit for nonpaid family caregivers.  Requires the Department of Taxation to submit annual reports to the Legislature.  Appropriates funds.  Applies to taxable years beginning after 12/31/2026.  Effective 1/1/2050.  (SD1)
bills.public_summary: Creates a state tax credit for unpaid family caregivers starting tax year 2027.

bills.title: RELATING TO HEALTH.
bills.description: Requires and appropriates funds for the State Health Planning and Development Agency to develop and publish a state plan on hearing loss.  (CD1)
bills.public_summary: Funds a state plan on hearing loss from the State Health Planning and Development Agency.

bills.title: RELATING TO KUPUNA HOUSING.
bills.description: Repeals the sunset for the State Rent Supplement Program for Kupuna.  Appropriates funds to the Hawaii Public Housing Authority for the State Rent Supplement Program for Kupuna and for two positions to support the program.  Effective 7/1/2050.  (SD1)
bills.public_summary: Makes the kupuna rent supplement program permanent and funds it with dedicated staff.
bills.last_action: The committee(s) on HOU/HHS has scheduled a public hearing on 03-19-26 1:06PM; Conference Room 225 & Videoconference.

bills.title: RELATING TO DEMENTIA.
bills.description: Requires the Hawaii Emergency Management Agency, fire chiefs, Law Enforcement Standards Board, and Department of Health to make available at least one hour of dementia‑specific training for first responders, including law enforcement officers, fire first responders, and emergency medical services personnel.  Requires the Executive Office on Aging to take certain steps when reviewing and recommending dementia-specific training curricula.  Effective 7/1/3000.  (SD1)
bills.public_summary: Requires dementia-specific training to be available for police, fire, and emergency responders.

bills.title: RELATING TO HEALTH.
bills.description: Requires the Department of Health to procure a Maternal and Infant Health Information Mobile Application by 1/1/2027 to provide qualified individuals with information on federal and state programs and resources for prenatal, pregnant, and postpartum individuals and their families.  Requires DOH to issue a request for proposals.  Authorizes DOH to procure or otherwise contract for an existing mobile pregnancy application.  Appropriates funds.  Effective 7/1/3000.  (HD1)
bills.public_summary: Requires the Department of Health to launch a maternal and infant health information app by 2027.

bills.title: RELATING TO THE WEST HAWAII REGIONAL HEALTH CARE SYSTEM.
bills.description: Appropriates funds for the planning, design, site work, and construction of a new outpatient care center in North Kona.  Effective 7/1/3000.  (HD1)
bills.public_summary: Funds planning and construction of a new outpatient care center in North Kona.
bills.last_action: Reported from HLT (Stand. Com. Rep. No. 355-26) as amended in HD 1, recommending passage on Second Reading and referral to FIN.

bills.title: RELATING TO A CLEAN FUEL STANDARD.
bills.description: Requires the Department of Transportation to adopt rules by 1/1/2028 governing a clean fuel standard for alternative fuels in the State.  Requires reporting and public informational session requirements.  Effective 7/1/3000.  (HD2)
bills.public_summary: Requires state rules for a clean fuel standard for alternative fuels by 2028.

bills.title: RELATING TO THE LIQUOR TAX.
bills.description: Replaces the defined liquor categories subject to the liquor tax with alcohol-by-volume categories, but with a separate rate for beer manufactured by a small craft producer pub licensee.  Adjusts the liquor tax rates for inflation.  Effective 7/1/3000.  (HD2)
bills.public_summary: Taxes liquor by alcohol content rather than drink category, adjusts rates for inflation, and keeps a lower rate for small craft brewers.

bills.title: RELATING TO DEAF INDIVIDUALS.
bills.description: Authorizes deaf motor vehicle owners to register their vehicle as being owned by a deaf individual so that a deafness designation appears when a law enforcement officer accesses the motor vehicle's information.  Effective 7/1/3000.  (HD1)
bills.public_summary: Lets deaf drivers add a deafness designation to vehicle registration visible to police during stops.
bills.last_action: Reported from TRN (Stand. Com. Rep. No. 436-26) as amended in HD 1, recommending passage on Second Reading and referral to JHA.

bills.title: RELATING TO SERVICE ANIMALS.
bills.description: Requires sellers or providers of emotional support animals, as well as those issuing verifications of a disability-related need for an emotional support animal, to provide written notice of certain laws relating to emotional support animals.  Requires persons or businesses that sell or provide certificates, vests, or identification tags that identify an animal as an emotional support animal to provide to the buyer or recipient written notice of certain laws relating to emotional support animals.  Establishes penalties.
bills.public_summary: Requires sellers of emotional support animals and related certificates to give written notice of the law.
bills.last_action: Referred to CPC, JHA, referral sheet 3

bills.title: RELATING TO PARKING FOR PERSONS WITH DISABILITIES.
bills.description: Provides that people who are blind or deaf are eligible to apply for and receive a disabled paid parking permit.
bills.public_summary: Makes people who are blind or deaf eligible for disability parking permits.
bills.last_action: The committee(s) on HLT recommend(s) that the measure be deferred.

bills.title: RELATING TO HEARING AIDS.
bills.description: Exempts from the general excise tax, gross receipts from the sale of hearing aids received by a hospital, infirmary, medical clinic, health care facility, pharmacy, or a practitioner licensed to administer drugs to an individual.  Effective 7/1/3000.  (HD1)
bills.public_summary: Exempts hearing aids sold through medical providers from the general excise tax.
bills.last_action: Reported from ECD (Stand. Com. Rep. No. 414-26), recommending referral to FIN.

bills.title: RELATING TO FIREWORKS.
bills.description: Imposes a statewide limitation on consumer fireworks, except by permit for use at cultural events.
bills.public_summary: Limits consumer fireworks statewide to permitted cultural events.

bills.title: RELATING TO CHILD WELL-BEING.
bills.description: Requires the Department of Human Services to establish and administer a Hawaii Rx kids program to improve the economic stability of households with very young children who reside in the State through a one-time payment and several monthly payments.
bills.public_summary: Creates a program providing direct cash payments to Hawaii households with very young children.
bills.nickname: Cash support for families with babies
bills.last_action: The committee(s) on HSH recommend(s) that the measure be deferred.

bills.title: RELATING TO THE HOUSEHOLD AND DEPENDENT CARE SERVICES TAX CREDIT.
bills.description: Increases a taxpayer's applicable percentage of employment-related expenses that is used to calculate the household and dependent care services tax credit.  Establishes certain disallowance periods following a final decision that a claim for the credit was due to fraud and that the claim was disallowed.  Extends the sunset date of the temporary increase in maximum employment-related expenses that are used to calculate the household and dependent care services tax credit, established by Act 163, SLH 2023, to 6/30/2030.  Sunsets 6/30/2030.  Effective 1/1/2050.  (SD1)
bills.public_summary: Increases the tax credit for household and dependent care expenses.
bills.nickname: Bigger child and dependent care credit

bills.title: RELATING TO TAXATION.
bills.description: Establishes a new bracket for higher-income earners for taxable years beginning after 12/31/2029.
bills.public_summary: Creates a new income tax bracket for higher earners starting 2030.

bills.title: RELATING TO FAMILY CAREGIVER SUPPORT.
bills.description: Establishes a Disability and Caregiver Support Working Group to explore compliant and fiscally responsible approaches that address the longstanding gap affecting parents and guardians with disabilities whose caregiving capacity may be substantially impaired due to disability or serious medical conditions, while preserving federal funding integrity.  Requires a report to the Legislature.  Appropriates funds.  Effective 7/1/3000.  (SD1)
bills.public_summary: Creates a working group on support for parents and guardians whose disability affects their caregiving.

bills.title: RELATING TO TAXATION.
bills.description: Establishes a surcharge on taxable income exceeding $1,000,000 to provide funding, if approved by the Legislature, for the State Medicaid Program.
bills.public_summary: Adds a surcharge on income over one million dollars to help fund the state Medicaid program.
bills.last_action: The committee(s) on HSH recommend(s) that the measure be deferred.

bills.title: RELATING TO TRANSPORTATION.
bills.description: Establishes safe riding behaviors for electric bicycles.  Prohibits the operation of high-speed electric devices in certain locations.  Establishes labeling and signage requirements for electric bicycles.  Prohibits the operation of a moped or electric motorcycle in certain locations.  Amends the definition of "bicycle" for purposes of county vehicular taxes.  Defines "electric bicycle" in place of "low-speed electric bicycle".  Authorizes the seizure of non-road-legal or nonconforming electric bicycles and high-speed electric devices.  Defines "electric micro-mobility device" and requires the same regulations as electric foot scooters.  Prohibits a person under the age of sixteen from operating a class 2 or class 3 electric bicycle without direct supervision.  Authorizes a person to ride an electric bicycle on a sidewalk under certain circumstances.  Prohibits a person from operating a bicycle or electric foot scooter under the age of eighteen without a helmet.  Repeals the requirement that moped drivers use bicycle lanes.  Substitutes the term "motor scooter" with the term "motor-driven cycle".  (CD1)
bills.public_summary: Sets safe riding rules, labeling and signage for electric bicycles and limits where high-speed devices may go.
bills.last_action: The committee(s) on TRS/EIG has scheduled a public hearing on 03-17-26 3:05PM; Conference Room 229 & Videoconference.

bills.title: RELATING TO TRANSPORTATION AFFORDABILITY.
bills.description: Requires the Department of Transportation to establish a clean vehicle rebate program to provide rebates for the purchase or lease of new and used zero-emission vehicles and plug-in hybrid electric vehicles.  Establishes the clean vehicle special fund.  Beginning 1/1/2027, establishes a transportation affordability and energy security tax.  Effective 7/1/3000.  (HD2)
bills.public_summary: Creates a state rebate program for buying or leasing new and used electric and plug-in hybrid vehicles.

bills.title: RELATING TO TAXATION.
bills.description: PART II:  Exempts the sale of groceries and nonprescription drugs from the general excise tax.  PART III:  Removes the state income tax on unemployment compensation benefits.  PART IV:  Doubles the standard deduction for individuals earning less than $100,000 and joint filers earning less than $200,000.  Repeals the incremental increases on standard income tax deduction amounts.  PART V:  Increases the maximum adjusted gross income allowed to qualify for the low-income household renters' income tax credit and increases the credit amount.  PART VI:  Repeals the incremental changes to income tax brackets and removes the tax liability for the first $100,000 of individual income earned.
bills.public_summary: Exempts groceries and nonprescription drugs from the general excise tax and cuts several other taxes for working families.
bills.last_action: Referred to ECD, FIN, referral sheet 3

bills.title: RELATING TO TRANSPORTATION.
bills.description: Requires and appropriates funds for the Department of Transportation to establish a pilot program to offer fully subsidized public transit passes for department employees.  Requires a report to the Legislature.  Effective 7/1/3000.  (HD1)
bills.public_summary: Pilots fully subsidized bus passes for Department of Transportation employees.
bills.last_action: Passed Second Reading as amended in HD 1 and referred to the committee(s) on LAB with none voting aye with reservations; none voting no (0) and none excused (0).

bills.title: RELATING TO TRANSPORTATION.
bills.description: Requires the Department of Transportation to establish a Clean Transportation Alternatives Incentive Program that returns funds to eligible residents of the State who meet a certain income threshold or use a certain amount of gasoline as fuel for transportation.
bills.public_summary: Creates an incentive program returning clean transportation funds to lower-income residents.
bills.last_action: The committee(s) on TRN recommend(s) that the measure be deferred.

bills.title: RELATING TO TOBACCO PRODUCTS.
bills.description: Repeals existing law that preempted local ordinances or regulations that regulate the sale of cigarettes, tobacco products, and electronic smoking devices and nullified and voided any conflicting local laws and regulations.  Allows counties to adopt ordinances that regulate the sale of cigarettes, tobacco products, and electronic smoking devices that do not conflict with and are more stringent than the state law that govern smoking.
bills.public_summary: Lets counties pass their own rules on tobacco and e-cigarette sales by repealing state preemption.

bills.title: RELATING TO HOUSING.
bills.description: Restructures the conveyance tax to a marginal rate system for the sale of properties with residential use, adjusts the tax for multifamily properties to reflect value on a per-unit basis, and applies a cost-of-living adjustment to conveyance tax rates.  Allocates revenues from conveyance tax collections.  Allocates a portion of conveyance tax collections to the Dwelling Unit Revolving Fund to fund infrastructure programs in areas that meet minimum standards of transit-supportive density.  Allocates a portion of conveyance tax revenues to the Hawaii Agricultural Development Revolving Fund, Special Land and Development Fund, and Hawaiian Home Lands Infrastructure and Housing Special Fund.  Establishes and appropriates funds out of the Hawaiian Home Lands Infrastructure and Housing Special Fund.  Authorizes the Hawaii Agricultural Development Revolving Fund to be used to acquire land.  Effective 7/1/3000.  (SD1)
bills.public_summary: Restructures the conveyance tax on property sales with marginal rates and inflation adjustments.

bills.title: RELATING TO THE PSYCHOLOGY INTERJURISDICTIONAL COMPACT.
bills.description: Enacts, and authorizes the Governor to enter into, the Psychology Interjurisdictional Compact.
bills.public_summary: Joins the interstate compact letting licensed psychologists practice telehealth across state lines.
bills.last_action: Referred to HLT, CPC, JHA, referral sheet 3

bills.title: RELATING TO TOBACCO PRODUCTS.
bills.description: Repeals law that provides that all local ordinances or regulations that regulate the sale of cigarettes, tobacco products, and electronic smoking devices are preempted and that existing local laws and regulations conflicting with the state law on smoking are null and void.  Clarifies that counties retain the authority to adopt ordinances that regulate the sale of cigarettes, tobacco products, and electronic smoking devices, as long as the ordinances do not conflict with and are more stringent than the state law on smoking.
bills.public_summary: Restores county authority to regulate tobacco and e-cigarette sales more strictly than state law.
bills.last_action: Referred to HLT, CPC, FIN, referral sheet 3

bills.title: RELATING TO INTOXICATING LIQUOR.
bills.description: Establishes when unannounced visits and inspections may be conducted.  Repeals a category for dispenser licenses in which employees sit with patrons.  Clarifies the investigator's and police officer's authority to enter a liquor premises if they are denied admittance.
bills.public_summary: Updates liquor inspection rules, including when unannounced inspections may occur and investigator access rights.

bills.title: PROPOSING AN AMENDMENT TO THE HAWAII STATE CONSTITUTION TO PROHIBIT DESTRUCTIVE LIVE-FIRE MILITARY TRAINING ON PUBLIC LANDS.
bills.description: Proposes a constitutional amendment to prohibit destructive live-fire military training on State public trust lands.
bills.public_summary: Proposes a constitutional amendment banning destructive live-fire military training on state public trust lands.
bills.last_action: Referred to WAL/PBS, JHA, FIN, referral sheet 3

bills.title: RELATING TO RENT STABILIZATION.
bills.description: Establishes a statewide 3% annual limit on rent increases under chapter 521, Hawaii Revised Statutes.  Prohibits rent increases during the first 12 months of a tenancy and requires notice and certification for exempt properties.
bills.public_summary: Caps annual rent increases at three percent statewide and bans increases in the first year of tenancy.
bills.last_action: Referred to HSG, CPC, FIN, referral sheet 4

bills.title: RELATING TO HUMAN SERVICES.
bills.description: Establishes the Hawaii Benefits Hub Working Group to develop a plan for the governance and implementation of the Hawaii Benefits Hub and related referral, tracking, compliance, and coordination systems.  Requires reports to the Legislature.  Establishes a position within the Office of Enterprise Technology Services.  Appropriates funds.  Effective 7/1/3000.  (SD1)
bills.public_summary: Creates a working group to plan the Hawaii Benefits Hub, a single front door to state benefits.

bills.title: RELATING TO HUMAN SERVICES.
bills.description: Appropriates funds to the Department of Human Services to issue supplemental contracts to community-based organizations to address increases in costs related to labor, insurance, utilities, rent, and gas.  For any multi-year contracts entered into or renewed beginning in fiscal year 2027-2028, requires the Department of Human Services to issue a Request for Information to determine whether any existing contract remains fiscally sound and thereafter determine, with the consent of the contractor, whether a new request for proposals should be issued.  Effective 7/1/3000.  (SD1)
bills.public_summary: Funds cost-of-living supplements for community organizations under state human services contracts.
bills.last_action: The committee(s) on HHS has scheduled a public hearing on 03-18-26 1:00PM; CR 225 & Videoconference.

bills.title: RELATING TO GRANTS.
bills.description: Appropriates funds to the Office of Community Services (OCS) to award grants to certain nonprofit organizations.  Establishes an evaluation and selection committee to oversee the awarding of grants.  Requires an applicant for a grant to provide certain documentation on activities that qualify for community engagement hours to qualify for the grant.  Appropriates funds for positions in OCS and for the Department of the Attorney General to assist OCS in reviewing contracts and monitoring costs.  Effective 7/1/3000.  (HD2)
bills.public_summary: Funds grants to nonprofit organizations through the Office of Community Services with a new selection committee.
bills.last_action: The committee(s) on LBT has scheduled a public hearing on 03-18-26 3:00PM; Conference Room 225 & Videoconference.

bills.title: RELATING TO WASTE MANAGEMENT.
bills.description: Beginning 1/1/2027, prohibits the sale, offer for sale, or distribution for sale of any disposable electronic smoking devices in the State.  Establishes penalties.  Effective 1/30/2050.  (SD1)
bills.public_summary: Bans the sale of disposable e-cigarettes statewide starting January 1, 2027, with penalties for violations.
bills.last_action: The committee(s) on HHS/CPN has scheduled a public hearing on 03-20-26 9:30AM; Conference Room 229 & Videoconference.

bills.title: RELATING TO LOAN REPAYMENT FOR HEALTHCARE PROFESSIONALS.
bills.description: Appropriates funds for the Healthcare Education Loan Repayment Program.  Effective 7/1/3000.  (HD1)
bills.public_summary: Funds the health care education loan repayment program.

bills.title: RELATING TO MEDICAID.
bills.description: Requires the State Auditor to conduct audits of Medicaid health care insurance contractors and the Department of Human Services and its Med-QUEST division at least once every two years, with the first audits to be conducted by 1/1/2027, and the reports to be submitted no later than twenty days prior to the Regular Session of 2027.  Requires the Auditor to conduct audits.  Appropriates funds.
bills.public_summary: Requires the State Auditor to audit Medicaid contractors and Med-QUEST at least every two years.
bills.last_action: Referred to HSH, LMG, FIN, referral sheet 4

bills.title: RELATING TO HEALTH CARE.
bills.description: Establishes a universal, single payer health care system to be known as "Hawaii Care", to provide comprehensive health care benefits to all state residents and eventually replace all existing health care plans in the State.  Designates the Hawaii Health Authority as the responsible agency for the comprehensive planning, implementation, and administration of Hawaii Care.  Requires the Hawaii Health Authority to develop and submit a comprehensive implementation and administration plan to the legislature by a certain date.  Establishes the Hawaii Care special fund.  Requires the Hawaii Health Authority to adopt rules and submit reports to the Legislature.  Requires the Governor to appoint members to the Hawaii Health Authority by 12/31/2026.  Requires the Department of Human Services to apply for necessary federal waivers.  Takes effect 180 days after the approval of the Hawaii Medicaid State Plan and necessary federal waivers.  Appropriates funds.
bills.public_summary: Creates Hawaii Care, a universal single-payer health care system covering all state residents.
bills.last_action: Referred to HLT/HSH, CPC, FIN, referral sheet 5

bills.title: RELATING TO MEDICAID.
bills.description: Prohibits a financial risk-bearing entity from administering Medicaid services.  Requires the Department of Human Services to contract with one or more administrative services organizations to perform non-risk administrative functions for the operation of the State's Medicaid program.  Requires the Department to establish a Medicaid Care Coordination Program to contract with community-based programs to provide care coordination services.  Requires physicians, other independent practitioners, hospitals, and other institutional providers to be paid or reimbursed directly by the State's medicaid agency.  Requires the Department to establish regional health hubs in each county to serve as localized oversight bodies.  Requires the Department to convene a Medicaid Stakeholder Advisory Group to support continuous improvement throughout the transition period.  Requires reports to the Legislature.  Appropriate funds.
bills.public_summary: Bars financial risk-bearing entities from administering Medicaid, shifting to non-risk administrative contractors.
bills.last_action: Referred to HSH/HLT, CPC, FIN, referral sheet 5

bills.title: RELATING TO INSURANCE COVERAGE OF PROTON BEAM THERAPY.
bills.description: Beginning, 1/1/2027, requires health insurers, mutual benefit societies, and health maintenance organizations to provide coverage for medically necessary proton beam therapy for cancer treatment and prohibits imposing stricter clinical evidence standards on proton beam therapy than on other radiation treatments.
bills.public_summary: Requires insurers to cover medically necessary proton beam therapy for cancer without stricter evidence standards.
bills.last_action: Referred to HLT, CPC, referral sheet 5

bills.title: RELATING TO SUGAR-SWEETENED BEVERAGES.
bills.description: Establishes the sugar-sweetened beverage fee program.  Beginning 7/1/2027, imposes a 2 cent per fluid ounce fee on all sugar-sweetened beverages sold in the State and requires all distributors of sugar-sweetened beverages to register with the Department of Health.  On or after 6/30/27, prohibits retailers from selling or displaying for sale any sugar-sweetened beverage acquired from a distributor that is not registered with the Department of Health.  Requires management and performance audits. Requires annual reports to the Legislature.  Establishes the Healthy Ohana Advisory Committee.  Appropriates funds.
bills.public_summary: Charges a 2-cent-per-ounce fee on sugary drinks sold in Hawaii starting July 1, 2027.
bills.nickname: Sugary drink fee of 2 cents an ounce
bills.last_action: Referred to HLT, CPC/JHA, FIN, referral sheet 5

bills.title: RELATING TO THE ESTATE AND GENERATION-SKIPPING TRANSFER TAX.
bills.description: Establishes an unrealized gains surcharge on certain property transfers subject to the estate and generation-skipping transfer tax.  Except for certain types of properties within estates, lowers the applicable exclusion amount allowed.  Effective 7/1/3000.  (HD1)
bills.public_summary: Adds an unrealized gains surcharge to the estate tax and lowers the amount exempt from it.

bills.title: RELATING TO TAX HAVEN ABUSE.
bills.description: Part I:  Effective 1/1/2027, requires corporations to include in their income the income of all foreign subsidiaries to the State; applies the State's apportionment formula to determine the share of reported profits subject to the appropriate tax, which shall be deposited into the state general fund; and requires corporations to report all profits, losses, revenues, and inter-company transactions made and all taxes paid in other states.  Part II:  Establishes within DOTAX a Corporate Tax Law Task Force to annually review the State's corporate tax laws and recommend updates to close tax loopholes.
bills.public_summary: Requires corporations to report worldwide subsidiary income when calculating Hawaii taxes.
bills.last_action: Referred to ECD, FIN, referral sheet 5

bills.title: RELATING TO TAXATION.
bills.description: Disallows the dividends paid deduction for real estate investment trusts.
bills.public_summary: Ends the dividends paid deduction that lets real estate investment trusts avoid state income tax.
bills.last_action: Referred to ECD, CPC, FIN, referral sheet 5

bills.title: RELATING TO COMPLEX PATIENT TREATMENT.
bills.description: Appropriates funds to the Alcohol and Drug Abuse Division of the Department of Health to contract with community-based organizations for a behavioral health complex patient model.  Requires a report to the Legislature.
bills.public_summary: Funds community organizations to serve behavioral health patients with complex needs.
bills.last_action: Referred to HLT, FIN, referral sheet 5

bills.title: RELATING TO HEALTH CARE WORKFORCE DEVELOPMENT.
bills.description: Establishes positions and appropriates funds to the University of Hawaii to support health care workforce development in the State.  Effective 7/31/2055.  (SD1)
bills.public_summary: Funds positions at the University of Hawaii to develop the state health care workforce.

bills.title: RELATING TO CANCER.
bills.description: Repeals the requirement that a certain amount received from the cigarette tax on the wholesale price of each article or item of certain tobacco products deposited into the Hawaii Cancer Research Special Fund must be used for debt service of capital expenditures and building maintenance.  Appropriates funds for the University of Hawaii Cancer Center.  Effective 7/1/3000.  (HD1)
bills.public_summary: Frees Hawaii Cancer Research fund tobacco tax money from being restricted to building debt payments.
bills.last_action: Passed Second Reading as amended in HD 1 and referred to the committee(s) on HED with none voting aye with reservations; none voting no (0) and Representative(s) Holt excused (1).

bills.title: RELATING TO IMMUNIZATIONS.
bills.description: Requires, rather than authorizes, schools to provide an exemption from required immunizations.  Specifies that for purposes of the Department of Health's rulemaking authority and authority regarding infectious and communicable diseases, no child shall be subjected to medical examination, vaccination, revaccination, or immunization if a parent or legal guardian objects based on bona fide religious tenets and practices.
bills.public_summary: Requires schools to grant exemptions from student immunization requirements and limits state vaccination authority over children.
bills.last_action: Referred to HLT, EDN, JHA, referral sheet 5

bills.title: RELATING TO THE EDUCATION OF STUDENTS EXPERIENCING HOMELESSNESS.
bills.description: Requires the Department of Education to establish a program for the support of students experiencing homelessness.  Requires the Department to designate a state coordinator position and state navigator positions to implement the program.  Effective 7/1/3000.  (HD2)
bills.public_summary: Creates a Department of Education program with dedicated staff to support students experiencing homelessness.

bills.title: RELATING TO TRANSPORTATION.
bills.description: Requires, rather than authorizes, the Department of Education to develop and administer a Traffic Safety Education Program.  Requires the Department of Education's Traffic Safety Education program to include electric bicycles.  Effective 7/1/3000.  (HD2)
bills.public_summary: Makes the school traffic safety education program mandatory and adds electric bicycles to it.
bills.last_action: Reported from TRN (Stand. Com. Rep. No. 549-26) as amended in HD 2, recommending referral to FIN.

bills.title: RELATING TO HEALTH CARE.
bills.description: Prohibits health care facilities, health care providers, and emergency medical services from furnishing medical debt to a consumer credit reporting agency.  Prohibits consumer credit reporting agencies from reporting or maintaining medical debt information in the file on a consumer.  Effective 7/1/3000.  (HD1)
bills.public_summary: Bans medical debt from appearing on consumer credit reports.

bills.title: RELATING TO PAID FAMILY LEAVE.
bills.description: Provides state and county employees with five days of paid family leave each calendar year.
bills.public_summary: Gives state and county employees five days of paid family leave a year.

bills.title: RELATING TO PREDICTION MARKETS.
bills.description: Amends the definition of "gambling" to include predictive markets involving the purchase, sale, or financial speculation of securities, commodities, or other similar financial products on the outcome or future contingent event related to catastrophe, contests, death, legislation, national security, people, politics, and sports.  Effective 7/1/3000.  (HD2)
bills.public_summary: Classifies betting on predictive markets tied to events like disasters and elections as illegal gambling.

bills.title: RELATING TO HEALTH CARE.
bills.description: Amends the Healthcare Preceptor Tax Credit to remove language limiting access only to those practicing in primary care, to add licensed dietitians, physician assistants, and social workers as eligible preceptors and students, and to include residency and followship programs.  Adds the Director of Health and a representative of residency programs with eligible students to the Preceptor Credit Assurance Committee.  Applies to taxable years beginning after 12/31/2026.
bills.public_summary: Expands the health care preceptor tax credit to dietitians, physician assistants, and social workers beyond primary care.
bills.nickname: Tax credit for training health students
bills.last_action: Referred to HLT, FIN, referral sheet 5

bills.title: RELATING TO FOOD SECURITY.
bills.description: Establishes and appropriates funds in the form of grants for the Hawaii Farm to Families Program under the Department of Human Services to alleviate food shortages in the State.  Requires reports to the Legislature.  (SD1)
bills.public_summary: Creates and funds the Hawaii Farm to Families Program to ease food shortages in the state.

bills.title: RELATING TO TAX CREDITS.
bills.description: Establishes a refundable diaper tax credit.  Applies to taxable years beginning after 12/31/2025.  Effective 7/1/3000.  (HD2)
bills.public_summary: Creates a refundable tax credit for diaper costs.

bills.title: RELATING TO CASINO GAMING.
bills.description: Authorizes limited casino gaming in a single location in the City and County of Honolulu.  Establishes the Hawaii Gaming Control Commission.  Imposes a wagering tax on the monthly gross receipts received from casino gaming.  Establishes the State Gaming Fund.  Requires the Hawaii Gaming Commission to create and implement a Compulsive Gamblers Program.  Exempts the construction of any casino facility from county special assessments and certain special improvement district requirements.  Establishes certain civil service exemptions.  Appropriates funds with certain conditions.
bills.public_summary: Legalizes a single casino in Honolulu, with a state gaming commission and wagering tax.
bills.last_action: Referred to ECD, CPC/JHA, FIN, referral sheet 5

bills.title: RELATING TO MEDICAID.
bills.description: Repeals a provision in Act 4, Special Session Laws of Hawaii 2005, that prohibits the Department of Human Services from taking any action to remove pharmaceutical benefits management from managed care plans that provide health care coverage for Hawaii Medicaid beneficiaries.  Effective 7/1/3000.  (HD1)
bills.public_summary: Lets the state remove pharmacy benefit management from Medicaid managed care plans.
bills.last_action: Passed Second Reading as amended in HD 1 and referred to the committee(s) on FIN with none voting aye with reservations; none voting no (0) and none excused (0).

bills.title: RELATING TO HEALTH.
bills.description: Prohibits discrimination against a pharmacy or pharmacist with respect to participation, referral, reimbursement of a covered service, or indemnification.  Establishes beneficiary cost sharing and deductible requirements for prescription drugs.  Establishes minimum rates for which pharmacy benefit managers are to reimburse pharmacies for dispensing prescription drugs.  For prescription drug benefit plans executed, amended, adjusted, or renewed on or after 7/1/2027, requires a pharmacy benefit manager to use pass-through pricing, or may alternatively use spread pricing if any savings realized by the pharmacy benefit manager are passed on.
bills.public_summary: Bans discrimination against pharmacies in insurance networks and sets minimum reimbursement rules.
bills.last_action: Referred to HLT, CPC, referral sheet 5

bills.title: RELATING TO INSURANCE.
bills.description: Authorizes the Attorney General to bring a civil action in the name of the people of the State as parens patriae against any responsible party to recover certain costs or obtain certain relief, including costs and losses incurred by the Hawaii Property Insurance Association, Hawaii Hurricane Relief Fund, or other state entities, resulting from climate attributable harm or costs for risk of future climate attributable harm.  Authorizes the Hawaii Property Insurance Association and Hawaii Hurricane Relief Fund, or any private insurer licensed in the State to bring a civil cause of action against a responsible party to recover its costs and losses resulting from climate attributable harm.
bills.public_summary: Lets the Attorney General sue responsible parties to recover disaster-related state insurance costs.
bills.last_action: Referred to CPC, JHA, FIN, referral sheet 5

bills.title: RELATING TO CLEAN WATER.
bills.description: Preserves, as state law, water quality, permitting, and aquatic resource protections that are at least as protective as federal Clean Water Act regulations and standards in effect as of January 1, 2026, and ensures their continued applicability regardless of subsequent federal amendments, repeals, or reductions.
bills.public_summary: Locks federal Clean Water Act protections into state law even if federal standards are weakened.
bills.last_action: The committee(s) on EEP recommend(s) that the measure be deferred.

bills.title: RELATING TO THE SUPPLEMENTAL NUTRITION ASSISTANCE PROGRAM-EDUCATION PROGRAM.
bills.description: Appropriates funds to the University of Hawaii College of Tropical Agriculture and Human Resilience and the Department of Health to continue their implementation of the Hawaii Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program–Education Program.  Effective 7/1/3000.  (HD1)
bills.public_summary: Funds the continued statewide SNAP-Education nutrition program at the University of Hawaii and Department of Health.

bills.title: RELATING TO PUBLIC ASSISTANCE.
bills.description: Allows the Department of Human Services to administer and provide public assistance to eligible residents of the State during a Governor-declared state of emergency.  Allows the Department of Human Services to expend funds from the Hawaii Hurricane Relief Fund.
bills.public_summary: Lets the state provide public assistance to residents during a governor-declared emergency, using hurricane relief funds.
bills.last_action: The committee(s) on HSH recommend(s) that the measure be deferred.

bills.title: RELATING TO TOBACCO ENFORCEMENT.
bills.description: Clarifies that untaxed tobacco products are subject to forfeiture as contraband, without regard to the procedures set forth in Hawaii's asset forfeiture law in the same manner as untaxed cigarettes.  Confirms the authority of the Department of Taxation and the Department of the Attorney General to inspect and seize tobacco products, including electronic smoking devices and e-liquids.  Effective 7/1/3000.  (HD1)
bills.public_summary: Makes untaxed tobacco products subject to seizure as contraband, matching the rules for untaxed cigarettes.
bills.last_action: Reported from JHA (Stand. Com. Rep. No. 466-26) as amended in HD 1, recommending passage on Second Reading and referral to FIN.

bills.title: RELATING TO HEALTH CARE.
bills.description: Adopts the Uniform Health Care Decisions Act (2023), as modified, to replace existing chapters related to advance health care directives and advance mental health care directives.
bills.public_summary: Adopts the updated Uniform Health Care Decisions Act governing advance directives.
bills.last_action: Referred to HLT, JHA, referral sheet 5

bills.title: RELATING TO MENTAL HEALTH INTERVENTION.
bills.description: Requires the Director of Law Enforcement to adopt rules establishing training and certification standards and procedures for crisis intervention officers.  Clarifies the scope of treatment allowable under orders for assisted community treatment.  Requires the Department of the Attorney general to assist with the preparation, filing, and presentation of any request for a court or administrative order authorizing treatment over the objection of certain patients.
bills.public_summary: Sets training and certification standards for crisis intervention officers and clarifies assisted community treatment.
bills.last_action: Referred to HLT, JHA, referral sheet 5

bills.title: RELATING TO THE EMERGENCY AND BUDGET RESERVE FUND.
bills.description: Appropriates moneys out of the Emergency and Budget Reserve Fund for fiscal year 2026-2027 to maintain the levels of programs determined to be essential to education, public health, and public welfare, to provide for counter cyclical economic and employment programs of economic downturn, to restore facilities destroyed or damaged or services disrupted by disaster, and to meet other emergencies declared by the Governor or determined to be urgent by the Legislature.  Effective 7/1/3000.  (HD1)
bills.public_summary: Draws on the state emergency reserve to maintain essential education, health, and welfare programs.

bills.title: RELATING TO ENERGY ASSISTANCE.
bills.description: Establishes the Hawaii Home Energy Assistance Program within the Department of Human Services to assist qualifying households in paying their energy bills.  Requires the Public Utilities Commission Public Benefits Fee Administrator to provide certain information and assistance to recipients of the program.  Appropriates funds to implement the program.  Effective 7/1/3000.  (HD1)
bills.public_summary: Creates a state program helping qualifying households pay their energy bills.
bills.last_action: Report adopted; referred to the committee(s) on FIN with Representative(s) Alcos, Shimizu voting aye with reservations; Representative(s) Garcia, Pierick voting no (2) and Representative(s) Quinlan excused (1).

bills.title: RELATING TO THE NURSE LICENSURE COMPACT.
bills.description: Allows the Governor to enter the State into the multistate Nurse Licensure Compact, which will allow a nurse who is licensed by a home state to practice under a multistate licensure privilege in each party state, effective 1/1/2027.  Beginning 1/1/2027, allows the State Board of Nursing to charge different fees for registered nurses and licensed practical nurses who hold a multistate license issued by the State.  Appropriates general revenues.
bills.public_summary: Joins Hawaii to the multistate Nurse Licensure Compact, so a nurse licensed elsewhere may practice here.
bills.last_action: Referred to HLT/LAB, CPC, FIN, referral sheet 5

bills.title: RELATING TO THE PHYSICIAN ASSISTANT LICENSURE COMPACT.
bills.description: Authorizes the Governor to enter the PA Licensure Compact to create a comprehensive process that complements the existing licensing authority of the state medical board and provides a streamlined process that allows a PA to become licensed in multiple states, thereby enhancing the portability of a PA license and ensuring the safety of patients.
bills.public_summary: Joins the interstate compact streamlining physician assistant licensing across states.
bills.last_action: Referred to HLT/LAB, CPC, FIN, referral sheet 5

bills.title: RELATING TO SCHOOL MEALS.
bills.description: Requires the Department of Education to charge not less than one-quarter of the cost of preparing a school meal for each school meal.  (SD2)
bills.public_summary: Lowers the minimum price schools must charge for meals from half to one-quarter of the cost of preparation.
bills.nickname: Lower minimum price for school meals

bills.title: RELATING TO DEPARTMENT OF EDUCATION PROCUREMENT.
bills.description: Adjusts the applicability of Act 134, SLH 2025, to clarify the threshold for Department of Education procurement of local edible produce and packaged food products.  Prohibits the artificial division and parceling of DOE procurements of local edible produce and packaged food products.  Sunsets 6/30/2028.  (CD1)
bills.public_summary: Clarifies when schools must buy local produce and food, and bars splitting purchases up to get around the rule.
bills.nickname: Local food buying rules for schools
bills.last_action: The committee(s) on EDU has scheduled a public hearing on 03-18-26 1:00PM; Conference Room 229 & Videoconference.

bills.title: RELATING TO INCOME TAX.
bills.description: Repeals future adjustments to income tax brackets.  For taxable years beginning after 12/31/2026, increases the income tax rates for the three highest income tax brackets by one percentage point each.  Increases a taxpayer's applicable percentage of employment-related expenses that is used to calculate the household and dependent care services tax credit.  Establishes certain disallowance periods following a final decision that a claim for the credit was due to fraud and that the claim was disallowed.  Extends the sunset for amendments made by Act 163, SLH 2023, to the Household and Dependent Care Services Tax Credit, Earned Income Tax Credit, and Food/Excise Tax Credit.  Effective 7/1/3000.  (HD1)
bills.public_summary: Raises income tax rates on the three highest brackets and expands the dependent care tax credit.
bills.nickname: Higher income tax on top brackets

bills.title: MAKING AN EMERGENCY APPROPRIATION TO THE DEPARTMENT OF HUMAN SERVICES.
bills.description: Part I:  Provides an emergency appropriation to the Department of Human Services to replace general fund appropriations redirected to provide emergency food assistance during the 2025 federal government shutdown.  Part II:  Appropriates funds to supplement premium contributions due to participating health plans.  (CD1)
bills.public_summary: Provides emergency funding to replace food assistance money spent during the 2025 federal government shutdown.
bills.nickname: Emergency funds for shutdown food aid

bills.title: RELATING TO PREVENTIVE MEDICINE.
bills.description: Establishes the Hawaii Preventive Services Advisory Committee and authorizes the Department of Health to issue preventive service recommendations.  Requires health insurance coverage without cost-sharing for Department of Health-recommended clinical preventive services.  Provides immunity for healthcare providers' and facilities' provision of recommended clinical preventive services.
bills.public_summary: Creates a state preventive services committee and requires insurers to cover its recommendations with no cost sharing.
bills.last_action: Referred to HLT, CPC, JHA, referral sheet 5

bills.title: RELATING TO EMERGENCY MEDICAL SYSTEMS OF CARE.
bills.description: Modernizes Hawaii's emergency medical services laws to align with current best practices and adopt a time-sensitive emergency medical systems of care model.  Expands the Community Paramedicine Program to include integrated mobile health care; permit additional partnerships with professional organizations and educational institutions; and authorize certain telehealth services by providers located in or out of the State, under certain circumstances.  Renames the State Emergency Medical Services Advisory Council the Hawaii Emergency Medical Systems of Care Advisory Council and amends its membership.  (CD1)
bills.public_summary: Modernizes emergency medical services laws and expands community paramedicine into mobile health care.
bills.last_action: The committee(s) on HHS has scheduled a public hearing on 03-18-26 1:00PM; CR 225 & Videoconference.

bills.title: RELATING TO LEAD MATERIALS IN WATER INFRASTRUCTURE.
bills.description: Amends prohibitions on the use of lead materials in drinking water distribution to align with the Safe Drinking Water Act and related Code of Federal Regulations.
bills.public_summary: Aligns Hawaii's lead-in-drinking-water rules with federal safe drinking water standards.
bills.last_action: Passed Second Reading and referred to the committee(s) on JHA with none voting aye with reservations; none voting no (0) and none excused (0).

bills.title: RELATING TO THE STATE HEALTH PLANNING AND DEVELOPMENT AGENCY.
bills.description: Amends the functions and responsibilities of the State Health Planning and Development Agency.  Adds a new definition of "health care" for the purposes of health planning and resource development and health care cost control.  Increase the certificate of need exemption threshold for bed changes to up to thirty per cent of existing licensed beds.  Exempts health care facilities or services operated by the Department of Health from certificate of need requirements.  (CD1)
bills.public_summary: Updates state health planning laws and raises the certificate of need exemption threshold.
bills.last_action: The committee(s) on HHS has scheduled a public hearing on 03-18-26 1:00PM; CR 225 & Videoconference.

bills.title: RELATING TO DANGEROUS INTOXICATION.
bills.description: Establishes the offenses of dangerous intoxication and habitual dangerous intoxication.  Provides for civil protective custody and transport for emergency examination under section 334-45, HRS, in lieu of arrest for dangerous intoxication in specified circumstances, and bars prosecution when civil protective custody is used.  Requires probation with mandatory treatment for habitual dangerous intoxication, with incarceration only upon probation violation.  Makes conforming amendments to chapter 334, HRS.
bills.public_summary: Creates dangerous intoxication offenses with civil protective custody as an alternative to arrest.

bills.title: MAKING AN EMERGENCY APPROPRIATION TO THE UNIVERSITY OF HAWAII.
bills.description: Makes an emergency appropriation for fiscal year 2025–2026 to the University of Hawaii to expand and sustain the Maui Wildfire Exposure Study and Maui Health Registry.  Effective 7/1/3000.  (HD1)
bills.public_summary: Provides emergency funding to expand and sustain the Maui Wildfire Exposure Study and health registry.
bills.nickname: Funding for Maui wildfire health study

bills.title: RELATING TO PAID FAMILY LEAVE.
bills.description: By 1/1/2029, requires the Department of Labor and Industrial Relations to establish a family and medical leave insurance program and begin collecting payroll contributions to finance payment of benefits.  By 1/1/2030, requires the Department to begin receiving claims and paying benefits under the program.  Specifies eligibility requirements and employee protections under the program.  Excludes paid family and medical leave benefits from income tax.  Effective 7/1/3000.  (HD2)
bills.public_summary: Creates a statewide paid family and medical leave insurance program, with benefits beginning by 2030 and benefits exempt from income tax.

bills.title: RELATING TO HEALTH.
bills.description: Prohibits the imposition of cost-sharing requirements for certain diagnostic and supplemental breast examinations.
bills.public_summary: Bars copays and deductibles on diagnostic and supplemental breast examinations.
bills.last_action: Referred to HLT, CPC, referral sheet 6

bills.title: PROPOSING AN AMENDMENT TO ARTICLE IX OF THE HAWAII STATE CONSTITUTION RELATING TO WAGE EQUITY.
bills.description: Proposes an amendment to Article IX of the Hawaii State Constitution to guarantee that every person has the inalienable right, while engaged in employment in the State, to be paid at a wage rate that is at least equal to the state minimum wage rate, as provided by law, without regard to the type or nature of employment, unless justified by a compelling state interest achieved by the least restrictive means.
bills.public_summary: Proposes a constitutional amendment guaranteeing every worker at least the state minimum wage.
bills.last_action: Referred to LAB, JHA, FIN, referral sheet 6

bills.title: RELATING TO MEDICAID.
bills.description: Prohibits a financial risk-bearing entity from administering Medicaid services.  Requires the Department of Human Services to contract with one or more administrative services organizations to perform non-risk administrative functions for the operation of the State's Medicaid program.  Requires the Department to establish a Medicaid Care Coordination Program to contract with community-based programs to provide care coordination services.  Requires physicians, other independent practitioners, hospitals, and other institutional providers to be paid or reimbursed directly by the State's medicaid agency.  Requires the Department to establish regional health hubs in each county to serve as localized oversight bodies.  Requires the Department to convene a Medicaid Stakeholder Advisory Group to support continuous improvement throughout the transition period.  Requires reports to the Legislature.  Appropriate funds.
bills.public_summary: Bars risk-bearing insurers from running Medicaid services and moves administration to non-risk contractors.
bills.last_action: Referred to HSH/HLT, CPC, FIN, referral sheet 6

bills.title: RELATING TO ASSISTED COMMUNITY TREATMENT.
bills.description: Authorizes registered nurses and qualified state-licensed health care professionals who are participating in a community paramedicine program approved by the Department of Health who are licensed by the State to administer medication as part of an assisted community treatment order's treatment plan to the subject of the order, under certain circumstances.  Effective 7/1/3000.  (HD1)
bills.public_summary: Lets nurses and licensed providers in community paramedicine programs administer court-ordered treatment medication.
bills.last_action: This measure has been deleted from the meeting scheduled on Wednesday 02-25-26 2:00PM in conference room 325 VIA VIDEOCONFERENCE.

bills.title: RELATING TO PUBLIC TRANSIT.
bills.description: Establishes a two-year Keiki Fare-Free Transit Pilot Program on Oahu and Kauai.  Appropriates funds.
bills.public_summary: Launches a two-year pilot letting kids ride public buses free on Oahu and Kauai.
bills.nickname: Free bus rides for keiki pilot
bills.last_action: The committee(s) on TRN recommend(s) that the measure be deferred.

bills.title: RELATING TO CHILD ABUSE.
bills.description: Amends the definition of "child abuse or neglect" to clarify that the failure to provide certain needs to a child shall not constitute child abuse or neglect if the sole reason the person responsible for the care of the child is unable to adequately provide for the child's care is lack of financial resources; and evidence of parental request for support shall not be deemed as evidence of child abuse and neglect.  Effective 7/1/3000.  (SD1)
bills.public_summary: Clarifies that poverty alone does not make a parent's inability to provide for a child count as abuse or neglect.
bills.nickname: Poverty alone is not child neglect

bills.title: RELATING TO OVERDOSE PREVENTION.
bills.description: Establishes and provides criteria for overdose prevention centers, including standards for the Department of Health to designate certain facilities as overdose prevention centers.  Establishes an Overdose Prevention Center Oversight Committee. Provides immunity from state criminal prosecution for certain offenses for persons using a designated overdose prevention center and persons operating a designated overdose prevention center.
bills.public_summary: Authorizes state-designated overdose prevention centers with oversight and immunity from state criminal liability.

bills.title: RELATING TO NET INVESTMENT INCOME TAX.
bills.description: Establishes a net investment income tax.
bills.public_summary: Creates a state tax on net investment income.

bills.title: RELATING TO THE DEPARTMENT OF HUMAN SERVICES.
bills.description: Appropriates funds for the Department of Human Services to collaborate with contracted community-based organizations to address the need for social services in the State.  Effective 12/31/2050.  (SD1)
bills.public_summary: Funds the Department of Human Services to work with community organizations on unmet social service needs.

bills.title: RELATING TO TAXATION.
bills.description: Increases the income eligibility limit and credit amount per exemption claimed for the income tax credit for low-income household renters.  Effective 7/1/3000.  (HD3)
bills.public_summary: Raises the income limit and credit amount for the low-income household renters tax credit.
bills.nickname: Bigger tax credit for low-income renters

bills.title: RELATING TO STUDENT SAFETY.
bills.description: Requires the Department of Education to develop, adopt, and implement a standardized emergency response plan governing immigration enforcement activity at or within one thousand feet of public schools and adopt policies and procedures to address immigration enforcement activity at certain school-related location and events.  Effective 7/1/3000.  (HD1)
bills.public_summary: Requires schools to adopt emergency response plans for immigration enforcement activity near campuses.
bills.last_action: The committee(s) on EDN recommend(s) that the measure be deferred.

bills.title: RELATING TO THE WAGE AND HOUR LAW.
bills.description: Authorizes the Department of Labor and Industrial Relations to establish a Community Wage Theft Enforcement Partnership Program and enter into contracts or memoranda of agreements with community-based organizations to enhance outreach, referral, and recovery of stolen wages.  Appropriates funds.  Effective 7/1/3000.  (HD1)
bills.public_summary: Funds community partnerships helping workers recover stolen wages.
bills.last_action: The committee(s) on JHA recommend(s) that the measure be deferred.

bills.title: RELATING TO STUDENT HEAT EXPOSURE SAFETY.
bills.description: Requires the Department of Education, in collaboration with the Department of Health and State Public Charter School Commission, to conduct a study on the current practices of managing heat exposure in state public and charter schools to protect students' health during outdoor activities and to develop a plan if the current practices are insufficient in managing heat exposure.  Effective 7/1/3000.  (HD1)
bills.public_summary: Orders a study of how public schools manage student heat exposure during outdoor activities, with a plan to close the gaps.

bills.title: RELATING TO TRANSPORTATION.
bills.description: Beginning 1/1/2027, requires each county to implement fare-free access to its public transportation systems.  Establishes the Fare-Free Public Transportation Tax and Dividend Special Fund.  Increases the Environmental Response, Energy, and Food Security Tax on petroleum products to fund fare-free public transportation.  Effective 7/1/3000.  (HD1)
bills.public_summary: Makes county public transportation fare-free statewide starting 2027, funded by a higher petroleum products tax.
bills.last_action: The committee(s) on EEP recommend(s) that the measure be deferred.

bills.title: RELATING TO EMPLOYMENT PRACTICES.
bills.description: Requires certain employers to provide administrative leave of absence for victims of workplace violence or threat of workplace violence.  Expands the type of certification an employee may provide to an employer if the leave exceeds five days per calendar year.  Prohibits retaliation against employees for exercising rights related to domestic violence, sexual violence, or workplace violence or threat of workplace violence.  Effective 1/1/2077.  (SD1)
bills.public_summary: Requires certain employers to give leave to victims of workplace violence and bars retaliation.

bills.title: RELATING TO DRUGS FOR WEIGHT LOSS.
bills.description: Requires the Department of Human Services to provide Medicaid prescription drug program recipients with coverage of glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) drugs for weight loss.  Appropriates funds.  (HD1)
bills.public_summary: Requires Hawaii Medicaid to cover GLP-1 drugs for weight loss.
bills.last_action: Reported from HSH/HLT (Stand. Com. Rep. No. 382-26) as amended in HD 1, recommending passage on Second Reading and referral to FIN.

bills.title: RELATING TO SURVEILLANCE PRICING.
bills.description: Requires the Office of Consumer Protection of the Department of Commerce and Consumer Affairs to conduct a study to determine the extent to which companies operating in the State deploy surveillance pricing practices.  Requires a report to the Legislature.  Appropriates funds.  Effective 1/1/2077.  (SD1)
bills.public_summary: Funds a state study of how companies use surveillance-based pricing on Hawaii consumers.
bills.nickname: Study of prices based on personal data

bills.title: RELATING TO CARDIOVASCULAR SCREENING.
bills.description: Requires cardiovascular screening for students, including student athletes.  Requires the Department of Education, in collaboration with the Department of Health, to distribute educational and informational materials regarding sudden cardiac arrest.  Requires the Department of Health to implement policies, programs, training, and continuing education that increase health care provider knowledge of cardiovascular screening guidelines.
bills.public_summary: Requires cardiovascular screening for students, including athletes, and education on sudden cardiac arrest.
bills.last_action: The committee(s) on EDN recommend(s) that the measure be deferred.

bills.title: RELATING TO ASSISTED COMMUNITY TREATMENT.
bills.description: Clarifies that community mental health outpatient programs that have agreed to provide mental health services to a defendant as part of an assisted community treatment order may prepare a certificate for assisted community treatment and provide the certificate to a defendant and may file an assisted community treatment petition with the Family Court.  (CD1)
bills.public_summary: Lets community mental health programs certify patients for court-ordered assisted treatment.
bills.last_action: The committee(s) on HHS has scheduled a public hearing on 03-18-26 1:00PM; CR 225 & Videoconference.

bills.title: RELATING TO THE MINIMUM WAGE.
bills.description: Amends the minimum monthly guaranteed compensation an individual must earn to be exempt from certain wage and hour requirements.  Requires the minimum wage to increase to $18.00 per hour beginning 1/1/2027, instead of 1/1/2028.  Increases the minimum wage on 1/1/2028, 1/1/2029, and 1/1/2030.  Prohibits tipped employees from being paid less than the minimum wage.  Beginning on 9/30/2030, and on September 30 of each year thereafter, requires the Department of Labor and Industrial Relations to calculate an adjusted minimum wage rate.
bills.public_summary: Raises the minimum wage to 18 dollars an hour starting 2027, a year earlier than scheduled, with further annual increases.
bills.last_action: Referred to LAB, FIN, referral sheet 6

bills.title: RELATING TO LIQUOR LICENSES.
bills.description: Authorizes an increase in the volume of manufactured alcoholic beverages permissible under a small craft producer pub license.  Increases the amount of alcohol manufactured on small craft producer pub licensees' premises that may be sold in recyclable containers.
bills.public_summary: Raises production and container sales limits for small craft brewery pubs.
bills.last_action: Referred to ECD, CPC, referral sheet 6

bills.title: RELATING TO LAW ENFORCEMENT.
bills.description: Prohibits with certain exceptions, the use of facial coverings and requires visible identification by law enforcement officers and their vehicles in the performance of their duties.  Requires state and county law enforcement agencies to establish policies regarding state and county cooperation with federal civil immigration enforcement.  Prohibits law enforcement officers from prolonging a stop to inquire about a person's civil immigration status.  Establishes criminal offenses for use of a mask or facial covering by a law enforcement officer, lack of visible identification, and unauthorized civil immigration arrest or detention.  Effective 3/22/2075.  (SD2)
bills.public_summary: Requires police to show visible ID, bars face coverings on duty, and sets rules on cooperation with federal immigration enforcement.
bills.nickname: Police must show ID, no face coverings
bills.last_action: The committee(s) on PSM/EIG has scheduled a public hearing on 03-23-26 3:00PM; Conference Room 016 & Videoconference.

bills.title: RELATING TO SPORTS WAGERING.
bills.description: Allows for the regulation of sports wagering by the Department of Business, Economic Development, and Tourism.  Establishes licensing requirements for sports wagering operators and sports wagering suppliers.  Establishes a general excise tax to be levied on sports wagering operator licenses.  Establishes the Problem Gambling Prevention and Treatment Special Fund to be administered and expended by the Department of Health.  Specifies that legal sports wagering and fantasy sports contests shall not be considered contests of chance or gambling.  Authorizes the Department of Business, Economic Development, and Tourism to perform criminal history record checks on applicants and licensees relating to sports wagering.  Effective 7/1/3000.  (HD1)
bills.public_summary: Legalizes and regulates sports betting in Hawaii, with operator licensing, a state tax and a problem gambling treatment fund.
bills.last_action: Reported from ECD (Stand. Com. Rep. No. 263-26) as amended in HD 1, recommending passage on Second Reading and referral to JHA/CPC.

bills.title: RELATING TO GENERAL EXCISE TAX.
bills.description: Exempts food and groceries from the general excise tax.  Expands a 2024 session law exempting certain medical and dental services to include all medical and dental services.
bills.public_summary: Exempts food and groceries from the general excise tax and extends the exemption to all medical and dental care.

bills.title: RELATING TO THE HAWAII INVASIVE SPECIES COUNCIL.
bills.description: Appropriates funds for the Native Resources and Fire Protection Program and Hawaii Invasive Species Council to ensure their long-term viability and continue to control and eradicate invasive species in the State.  Effective 7/1/3000.  (SD1)
bills.public_summary: Funds the Hawaii Invasive Species Council and the state's native resources and fire protection work.

bills.title: RELATING TO ADAPTATION PATHWAYS PLANNING.
bills.description: Requires the Hawaii Climate Change Mitigation and Adaptation Commission to develop adaptation pathways plans to modify and relocate development and associated infrastructure away from critically vulnerable areas to locations outside of sea level rise and coastal flooding exposure area.  Appropriates funds.  Effective 7/1/3000.  (HD1)
bills.public_summary: Requires state plans for relocating development away from sea level rise and coastal flooding zones.

bills.title: RELATING TO MEDICAL CANNABIS.
