index.description: Prohibits state and local law enforcement agencies to collaborate with the federal government for immigration purposes except for in limited, specific circumstances.

index.title: RELATING TO SUPPORTED DECISION-MAKING AGREEMENTS.
index.description: Allows qualified adults, including adults with a disability, mentally ill adults, and adults sixty-five years of age or older, to enter into supported decision-making agreements with one or members of a supportive community.  Specifies the terms of a supported decision-making agreement, including access to personal information and agreement requirements.

index.title: RELATING TO COVERED OFFENDER REGISTRATION.
index.description: Amends covered offender registration laws to include offenders who, while acting in a professional capacity, commit the offense of sexual assault in the fourth degree against a minor who is at least sixteen years old.  Provides that the exception to public access requirements does not apply when the covered offense was committed against a minor.

index.title: RELATING TO SENTENCING.
index.description: Prohibits emerging adult defendants from being sentenced to life imprisonment without the possibility of parole.  (SD1)

index.title: RELATING TO THE DEFENSE OF STATE EMPLOYEES.
index.description: Requires the State to defend professionally licensed or certified state employees from civil actions or proceedings, under certain circumstances.  Clarifies that the employee may employ their own attorney at the employee's own expense.  Establishes a process for the Attorney General to transfer or withdraw representation if the Attorney General declines to defend the employee.

index.title: RELATING TO VOTER REGISTRATION.
index.description: Makes an application for voter registration part of certain state agency application processes.  Requires the sharing of certain information among certain state agencies, election personnel, and online voter registration system.

index.title: RELATING TO ELECTIONS.
index.description: Specifies that election ballots issued by the Chief Election Officer or county clerk shall exclude any candidate who is disqualified by a constitutional or statutory provision. index.description: Appropriates funds to support the Olelo Hawaii Initiatives.  Effective 4/23/2057.  (SD1)

index.title: RELATING TO HEALTH.
index.description: Requires Medicaid and private insurance coverage of ambulance services and community paramedicine services rendered statewide by emergency medical technicians or paramedics.  Appropriates funds.

index.description: Requires the Department of Education to establish a food waste composting pilot project at Nanakuli High and Intermediate School.  Appropriates moneys.

index.description: Establishes the offense of criminal street gang participation, solicitation, recruitment, or retention.  Provides for enhanced penalties for crimes committed by a defendant while part of a criminal street gang.

index.description: Requires condominiums and planned community associations to issue monthly damage and repair reports, have a reserve study done every 3 years, have a fully funded reserve, and only spend reserve funds to maintain the property.

index.description: Prohibits the Department of Land and Natural Resources and Board of Land and Natural Resources from disposing of or approving the use or setting aside of public lands for the establishment of any immigration detention facility. index.title: RELATING TO AUTOMOTIVE REPAIR.
index.description: Provides access by owners of motor vehicles and independent repair facilities to motor vehicle manufacturer diagnostic and repair information and diagnostic repair tools otherwise made available to dealers.

index.description: Requires managing agents for residential condominium properties with more than one hundred units located in a county with a population greater than 500,000 to possess a community association manager credential from a recognized nationwide community association management industry trade group. index.title: RELATING TO FOSTER CARE.
index.description: Prohibits the Department of Human Services from using any social security income payments, including supplemental income payments it receives on behalf of a child under foster custody of the Department to cover the cost of foster care services. index.title: RELATING TO CAPITAL IMPROVEMENT PROJECTS FOR THE BENEFIT OF THE FIFTEENTH SENATORIAL DISTRICT.
index.description: Appropriates funds for capital improvement projects in the 15th senatorial district.

index.title: RELATING TO LOW-SPEED ELECTRIC BICYCLES.
index.description: Increases the minimum age to operate a low-speed electric bicycle from fifteen to sixteen years of age.

index.title: RELATING TO A STATE HOTEL.
index.description: Requires the Hawaii Tourism Authority and School of Travel Industry Management at the University of Hawaii at Manoa to collaborate to actively plan for the design, construction, and operations and management of a state hotel.  Requires reports to the Legislature.  Appropriates funds.

index.title: RELATING TO SMALL BUSINESS LOANS.
index.description: Establishes the Hawaii Start-Up Business Loan Program within the Business Development and Support Division of the Department of Business, Economic Development, and Tourism.  Establishes the Hawaii Start-Up Business Loan Program Special Fund.  Requires DBEDT to submit annual reports to the Legislature.  Establishes one full-time equivalent business loan officer position.  Appropriates funds.  Effec

index.title: RELATING TO WATER POLLUTION.
index.description: Requires a landowner in possession of ten thousand or more acres in the State to be liable for damages and fines arising from runoff originating on the land and entering into state waters.  Requires the Department of Health to prioritize enforcement of water pollution control regulations in rural areas where there are existing reports of runoff and other terms of water pollution.  Effective 7/1/30

index.title: RELATING TO CONSUMER PROTECTION.
index.description: Establishes a new gift card fraud law, under the scope of unfair and deceptive practices law, which requires merchants and third-party gift card resellers to take certain steps to prevent gift card scams.  Requires the conspicuous provision of information regarding terms and conditions of gift certificates, regardless of whether the cards are sold in person, electronically, or telephonically.  Ext

index.title: RELATED TO TOURISM.
index.description: Amends the types of occurrences for which the Hawaii Tourism Authority Board of Directors may request the Governor to declare a tourism emergency.  Reduces the minimum balance to be maintained in the Tourism Emergency Special Fund through an allocation of transient accommodations tax revenues.  Effective 7/1/2050.  (SD1)

index.title: RELATING TO RECYCLING.
index.description: Allows manufacturers to coordinate activities directly related to the recycling of covered electronic devices.  Expands the scope of covered electronic devices to include electronic device peripherals and certain legacy devices.  Requires manufacturers to provide free collection service locations and collection events.

index.title: RELATING TO ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT.
index.description: Appropriates funds to the Hawaii Technology Development Corporation to assist small businesses with technology enablement and develop project management software to simplify the facilitated application process for small businesses.  Requires a report to the Legislature.  Effective 7/1/3000.  (HD1)

index.title: RELATING TO GOVERNMENT.
index.description: Allows a retirant to be employed without reenrollment in the Employees' Retirement System and without loss or interruption of retirement benefits if the retirant is employed as a school resource officer identified by the Department of Law Enforcement or other law enforcement agency as a labor shortage or difficult-to-fill position and stationed at a public school, subject to certain conditions.  E

index.title: RELATING TO SENTENCING.
index.description: Requires the court to impose a mandatory minimum term of imprisonment without possibility of parole or probation for a person convicted of a sexual assault offense.

index.title: RELATING TO LONG-TERM CARE.
index.description: Requires the Department of Health to conduct a study on the adequacy of long-term care on the island of Molokai.  Requires a report to the Legislature.  Appropriates funds.

index.title: RELATING TO THE HAWAII TECHNOLOGY DEVELOPMENT CORPORATION.
index.description: Requires the Hawaii Technology Development Corporation to establish state goals and implement projects to promote economic diversification through innovation and technology.  Requires annual reports to the Legislature.  Appropriates funds to the Small Business Innovation Research Program, Manufacturing Assistance Program, and Accelerator and Small Business Training Programs.  Effective 7/1/2050.

index.title: RELATING TO GEOTHERMAL ENERGY EXPLORATION.
index.description: Requires the Hawaii State Energy Office to conduct a statewide environmental assessment for, and subsequently administer, a Geothermal Resources Characterization Program under the direction of the Hawaii Groundwater and Geothermal Resources Center at the University of Hawaii.  Appropriates funds.

index.title: RELATING TO RENEWABLE FUEL.
index.description: Establishes the sustainable aviation fuel import tax credit.  Increases the renewable fuels production tax credit amount.  Repeals the:  (1) cap amount of claimable renewable fuels production tax credit; (2) requirement that the tax credit be claimed for fuels with lifecycle emissions below fossil fuels; and (3) prohibition on claiming other tax credits for the cost incurred to produce renewable f

index.title: RELATING TO RENEWABLE ENERGY.
index.description: Clarifies that adjustments linked to premium interest rates for high yield credit are just and reasonable.  Authorizes the Public Utilities Commission to include these incremental adjustments to the rate for electricity generated from nonfossil fuels.  (SD1)

index.title: RELATING TO ENERGY.
index.description: Requires an attestation or declaration regarding project labor standards, including adherence to state-approved apprenticeship programs and prevailing wage requirements, for covered large-scale renewable energy generation projects.  Effective 7/1/3000.  (HD1)

index.title: RELATING TO THE HAWAII FIRST RESPONDERS MEMORIAL.
index.description: Appropriates funds to the Department of Accounting and General Services to hire a consultant to evaluate potential locations and designs for the Hawaii First Responders Memorial.

REQUESTING THE DEPARTMENT OF BUSINESS, ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT, AND TOURISM TO SPONSOR A MICHELIN GUIDE FOR RESTAURANTS ACROSS THE STATE.

URGING THE SENATE TO ESTABLISH AN INVESTIGATIVE COMMITTEE PURSUANT TO CHAPTER 21, HAWAII REVISED STATUTES, TO INVESTIGATE ALLEGATIONS OF A 2022 CASH OR CHECK PAYMENT FROM AN UNKNOWN INDIVIDUAL TO AN “INFLUENTIAL LEGISLATOR” FOR THE PURPOSE OF INFLUENCING AN EXISTING POLITICAL CAMPAIGN, AND TO EXAMINE POSSIBLE VIOLATIONS OF STATE LAW, STATE ETHICS CODE, AND CAMPAIGN FINANCE PROVISIONS.
REQUESTING THE DIRECTOR OF HEALTH TO CONVENE A WATER FLUORIDATION WORKING GROUP.

REQUESTING THE DEPARTMENT OF THE ATTORNEY GENERAL TO CONVENE A YOUTH DIGITAL SAFETY AND PLATFORM ACCOUNTABILITY WORKING GROUP TO EXAMINE TECHNOLOGY-FACILITATED ABUSE IN THE STATE AND DEVELOP RECOMMENDATIONS FOR REGULATORY SAFEGUARDS.

URGING THE DEPARTMENT OF EDUCATION, IN CONSULTATION WITH THE DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH, TO CONDUCT A STUDY ON THE COST AND BENEFITS OF HIRING MENTAL HEALTH PROFESSIONALS FOR EVERY PUBLIC SCHOOL AND OF DISTRIBUTING GUIDELINES ON TELEHEALTH SAFE SPACES.

URGING THE DEPARTMENT OF EDUCATION, DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH, AND OFFICE OF WELLNESS AND RESILIENCE TO ESTABLISH A STATEWIDE PEER COUNSELOR PROGRAM TO ADDRESS YOUTH LONELINESS AND SOCIAL DISCONNECTION IN HAWAII'S SCHOOLS.
SUPPORTING THE DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH'S EFFORTS TO COORDINATE THE STOCKPILING OF A THREE-YEAR SUPPLY OF MIFEPRISTONE.

SUPPORTING THE USE OF THE DWELLING UNIT REVOLVING FUND TO FUND PREDEVELOPMENT COSTS FOR ANY GOVERNMENT AFFORDABLE HOUSING DEVELOPMENT PROJECT THROUGH INTERIM LOANS TO EXPEDITE THE DELIVERY OF AFFORDABLE HOUSING TO HAWAII'S RESIDENTS.
ESTABLISHING A SISTER-STATE RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN THE STATE OF HAWAII, UNITED STATES OF AMERICA, AND THE PREFECTURE OF OKAYAMA, JAPAN.
DECLARING THE INTENT THAT AFFORDABLE HOUSING CREDITS ARE PERPETUAL AND REMAIN VALID UNTIL REDEEMED, AND REQUESTING THE COUNTIES TO RECOGNIZE THESE CREDITS WITHOUT EXPIRATION DATES.
REQUESTING THE DEPARTMENT OF BUSINESS, ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT, AND TOURISM TO CONDUCT A STUDY ON HAWAII'S FOOD MANUFACTURING STRENGTHS AND STRATEGIC MARKETS.
ESTABLISHING THE HAWAII HEALTH PLAN WORKING GROUP TO DESIGN AND RECOMMEND A BASIC, AFFORDABLE HAWAII HEALTH PLAN AVAILABLE TO EVERY RESIDENT OF THE STATE.
URGING THE UNITED STATES CONGRESS TO PROVIDE OWNER-OCCUPANTS WITH COMPARABLY EQUIVALENT TAX DEDUCTIONS AFFORDED TO BUSINESS ENTITIES FOR EXPENSES RELATED TO PROPERTY OWNERSHIP.
REQUESTING THE DEPARTMENT OF EDUCATION TO REQUIRE ONE YEAR OF HAWAIIAN LANGUAGE INSTRUCTION AS A GRADUATION REQUIREMENT IN PUBLIC SCHOOLS.

REQUESTING THE ATTORNEY GENERAL TO CONDUCT A COMPREHENSIVE REVIEW OF THE HAWAII REVISED STATUTES TO IDENTIFY PROVISIONS IN WHICH THE TERM "IMPAIRED" OR A SIMILAR TERM IS USED TO DESCRIBE A PERSON WITH A DISABILITY AND TO SUGGEST DISABILITY-INCLUSIVE APPROPRIATE AMENDMENTS.
REQUESTING THE STATE FIRE MARSHAL TO APPOINT A HYDROGEN FIRE SAFETY EXPERT AND PROVIDE TRAINING ON HYDROGEN-RELATED SAFETY PROTOCOLS.
SUPPORTING THE FINDINGS AND RECOMMENDATIONS OF THE HAWAIʻI WATER SAFETY COALITION'S HAWAIʻI WATER SAFETY PLAN.
RECOGNIZING OPEN WATER LIFEGUARDS AS FIRST RESPONDERS IN ACKNOWLEDGEMENT OF THEIR ESSENTIAL ROLE IN EMERGENCY RESPONSE, PUBLIC SAFETY, AND COMMUNITY WELLBEING THROUGHOUT THE STATE.

ENDORSING TAIWAN'S INTERNATIONAL PARTICIPATION, SUPPORTING THE SIGNING OF A UNITED STATES-TAIWAN AGREEMENT ON AVOIDANCE OF DOUBLE TAXATION, AND COMMEMORATING THE SISTER-STATE RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN THE STATE AND TAIWAN.

URGING THE DIVISION OF BOATING AND OCEAN RECREATION OF THE DEPARTMENT OF LAND AND NATURAL RESOURCES TO DEVELOP A PROGRESSIVE ENFORCEMENT FRAMEWORK FOR PARKING VIOLATIONS IN PARKING LOTS UNDER ITS JURISDICTION; ENSURE PROPER USE OF PARKING AREAS BY INTENDED USERS; AND IMPROVE THE PREVALENCE AND CLARITY OF SIGNAGE REGARDING PARKING REGULATIONS, FEES, AND PENALTIES.

REQUESTING THE DISABILITY AND COMMUNICATION ACCESS BOARD TO STUDY THE COMMUNICATION NEEDS OF INDIVIDUALS WHO ARE DEAF, HARD OF HEARING, OR DEAF-BLIND IN HEALTH CARE SETTINGS AND MAKE NECESSARY REVISIONS TO THE GUIDANCE FOR HEALTH CARE PROVIDERS.

REQUESTING THE UNITED STATES CONGRESS TO ENACT LEGISLATION TO REMOVE CANNABIS FROM THE FEDERAL CONTROLLED SUBSTANCES ACT, PROVIDE SUPPORT TO STATES THAT ARE CLEARING DEFENDANTS' RECORDS OF CANNABIS OFFENSES, AND FACILITATE ACCESS TO THE FULL SPECTRUM OF BANKING SERVICES FOR CANNABIS-RELATED BUSINESSES.
REQUESTING THE GOVERNOR'S SENIOR ADVISOR FOR MENTAL HEALTH AND THE JUSTICE SYSTEM TO FORMULATE A PLAN TO INCREASE ACCESS TO THE HAWAII STATE HOSPITAL FOR CERTAIN MENTALLY ILL- CRIMINAL DEFENDANTS.
REQUESTING THE AUDITOR TO CONDUCT A PERFORMANCE AUDIT OF THE DEPARTMENT OF HAWAIIAN HOME LANDS.
REQUESTING THE DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH TO LEAD THE STATEWIDE COORDINATION OF SERVICES AND SUPPORT FOR INDIVIDUALS WITH FETAL ALCOHOL SPECTRUM DISORDERS.
REQUESTING THE DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORTATION TO CORRECT, UPDATE, AND COMPLETE ITS ADMINISTRATIVE RULES GOVERNING THE DRIVER EDUCATION PROGRAM AS RECOMMENDED BY THE AUDITOR'S REPORT NO. 25‑06.

REQUESTING THE DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORTATION AND DEPARTMENT OF LAND AND NATURAL RESOURCES TO COORDINATE THE TRANSFER OF SMALL BOAT HARBORS BACK TO THE DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORTATION AND TO ESTABLISH A MANAGEMENT TEAM TO DEVELOP TRANSITION PLANS.

URGING THE DEPARTMENT OF LAND AND NATURAL RESOURCES TO TRANSFER PARCELS THAT MAKE UP THE EAST KAPOLEI TRANSIT-ORIENTED DEVELOPMENT PROJECT TO THE HAWAII HOUSING FINANCE AND DEVELOPMENT CORPORATION AND URGING THE HAWAII HOUSING FINANCE AND DEVELOPMENT CORPORATION TO PARTNER WITH THE HAWAII COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT AUTHORITY TO FACILITATE THE DEVELOPMENT OF NON-HOUSING COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT PORTIONS OF THE PROJECT.
REQUESTING THE STATE AUDITOR TO CONDUCT A PERFORMANCE AUDIT OF THE HAWAII STATE BUILDING CODE COUNCIL.

REQUESTING THE DEPARTMENT OF EDUCATION TO PROVIDE FREE SCHOOL MEALS TO EVERY STUDENT ENROLLED IN A DEPARTMENT SCHOOL, REGARDLESS OF A STUDENT'S ELIGIBILITY FOR PARTICIPATION IN A FEDERAL SCHOOL MEALS PROGRAM, BEGINNING WITH THE 2029-2030 SCHOOL YEAR.
URGING THIS BODY TO INTRODUCE AND PASS LEGISLATION TO ESTABLISH STRICT LIABILITY FOR INDIVIDUALS WHO KEEP, HARBOR, OR FEED CERTAIN ANIMALS IN A MANNER THAT RESULTS IN DAMAGE TO PROPERTY.

REQUESTING THE DEPARTMENT OF LAND AND NATURAL RESOURCES AND BOARD OF LAND AND NATURAL RESOURCES TO EXEMPT ANY AGRICULTURAL ENTERPRISE PRACTICING DIVERSIFIED AGRICULTURE ON FORMER SUGARCANE LANDS WITHIN THE CONSERVATION DISTRICT FROM ANY REQUIREMENT FOR A PERMIT OR SIGHT PLAN APPROVAL GRANTED BY THE DEPARTMENT.

REQUESTING THE AUDITOR TO CONDUCT AN AUDIT OF NO-BID CONTRACTS ISSUED BY STATE AND COUNTY AGENCIES UNDER PROCLAMATIONS DECLARING STATES OF EMERGENCY DURING THE SIX-YEAR PERIOD BETWEEN JANUARY 1, 2020, AND DECEMBER 31, 2025.

URGING THE DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH TO LEAD A COORDINATED INTERDEPARTMENTAL EFFORT TO REDUCE THE IMPACT OF FETAL ALCOHOL SPECTRUM DISORDERS IN THE STATE, INCLUDING DEVELOPMENT OF A PLAN FOR INTERAGENCY COLLABORATION TO ENSURE THE COORDINATION OF SUPPORT SERVICES.

AFFIRMING AND SUPPORTING THE REQUIREMENT THAT HOSPITALS PROVIDE LIFE-SAVING EMERGENCY CARE TO PREGNANT PEOPLE, INCLUDING REPRODUCTIVE AND ABORTION SERVICES, WHEN SUCH CARE IS MEDICALLY NECESSARY TO STABILIZE A PATIENT UNDER THE EMERGENCY MEDICAL TREATMENT AND ACTIVE LABOR ACT.
REQUESTING THE DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORTATION AND DEPARTMENT OF LAW ENFORCEMENT TO COLLABORATE TO ESTABLISH A STATE HIGHWAY POLICE FORCE.

REQUESTING THE HAWAII STATE COMMISSION ON THE STATUS OF WOMEN, IN COLLABORATION WITH THE OFFICE OF THE LEGISLATIVE REFERENCE BUREAU AND DEPARTMENT OF THE ATTORNEY GENERAL, TO ESTABLISH A WORKING GROUP AND PROVIDE A REPORT TO THE LEGISLATURE ON WAYS TO STRENGTHEN PROTECTIONS FOR SURVIVORS OF IMAGE-BASED SEXUAL ABUSE.
ENCOURAGING THE DEPARTMENT OF EDUCATION TO OFFER A BASIC SWIMMING COURSE IN EITHER PRIMARY OR SECONDARY EDUCATION LEVELS.
REQUESTING THE CITY AND COUNTY OF HONOLULU TO CONSIDER DEVELOPING A FACILITY TO DISCARD LITHIUM-ION BATTERIES.

REQUESTING THE OFFICE OF PLANNING AND SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT, IN CONSULTATION WITH THE HAWAII COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT AUTHORITY, HAWAII HOUSING FINANCE AND DEVELOPMENT CORPORATION, AND THE CITY AND COUNTY OF HONOLULU, TO CONDUCT AN ASSESSMENT OF PROJECTED MAXIMUM INFRASTRUCTURE CAPACITY AROUND TRANSIT-ORIENTED DEVELOPMENT AREAS WITHIN THE CITY AND COUNTY OF HONOLULU.

REQUESTING THE DEPARTMENT OF HUMAN RESOURCES DEVELOPMENT TO COLLABORATE WITH STATE DEPARTMENTS, AGENCIES, AND LABOR ORGANIZATIONS IN COMPLETING THE COMPREHENSIVE REVIEW OF THE CLASSIFICATION AND COMPENSATION SYSTEMS FOR ALL CIVIL SERVICE POSITIONS UNDER ITS JURISDICTION.

REQUESTING THE OFFICE OF THE GOVERNOR TO EVALUATE AND MAKE RECOMMENDATIONS ON THE DECENTRALIZATION OF THE DEPARTMENT OF HUMAN RESOURCES DEVELOPMENT'S HIRING AND RECRUITMENT FUNCTIONS TO STATE DEPARTMENTS, DIVISIONS, AND AGENCIES, INCLUDING THE TRAINING OF HUMAN RESOURCES OFFICERS OF STATE DEPARTMENTS, DIVISIONS, AND AGENCIES NECESSARY TO EFFECTIVELY CARRY OUT THEIR HIRING AND RECRUITMENT FUNCTIONS.
REQUESTING ALL STATE AGENCIES TO UTILIZE BI-LEVEL LIGHTING SYSTEMS IN ALL STATE BUILDINGS AND FACILITIES, THE DESIGN OF WHICH IS FINALIZED ON OR AFTER JANUARY 1, 2028.
ENCOURAGING THE DEPARTMENT OF EDUCATION TO EXPAND THE HAWAIIAN IMMERSION PROGRAM.
ENCOURAGING THE STATE TO EXAMINE REQUIRING AUTOMATED EXTERNAL DEFIBRILLATORS IN ALL STATE-OWNED BUILDINGS AND PURSUE EXISTING AUTOMATED EXTERNAL DEFIBRILLATOR PROGRAMS.

URGING THE GOVERNOR TO TAKE ACTION TO PROTECT TRANSGENDER MEMBERS OF THE HAWAIʻI NATIONAL GUARD FROM DISCRIMINATORY FEDERAL POLICY AND PERMIT QUALIFIED TRANSGENDER SERVICE MEMBERS TO CONTINUE THEIR SERVICE.

REQUESTING THE DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORTATION TO COORDINATE WITH UTILITY PROVIDERS OPERATING WITHIN STATE HIGHWAY RIGHTS-OF-WAY TO DEVELOP A COMPREHENSIVE STATEWIDE PLAN AND SCHEDULE TO ADDRESS DERELICT OR AGING UTILITY POLES AND LINES ALONG FARRINGTON HIGHWAY AND OTHER HIGH-RISK CORRIDORS.
ENCOURAGING THE UNITED STATES NAVY TO TAKE RESPONSIBILITY FOR THE ERADICATION OF OCTOCORAL AND OTHER INVASIVE SPECIES FROM THE WATERS OF PEARL HARBOR, INCLUDING WEST LOCH, MIDDLE LOCH, AND EAST LOCH.
URGING THE DEPARTMENT OF EDUCATION TO STRENGTHEN MENSTRUAL HEALTH EDUCATION INITIATIVES AND TO ADOPT A COMPREHENSIVE MENSTRUAL CYCLE CURRICULUM.

REQUESTING THE DEPARTMENT OF CORRECTIONS AND REHABILITATION TO ESTABLISH A COORDINATED DATA ENTRY SYSTEM FOR THE DEPARTMENT OF CORRECTIONS AND REHABILITATION AND COUNTY POLICE DEPARTMENTS AND PROSECUTORS TO TRACK THE STATUS OF DETAINEES INCARCERATED IN DEPARTMENT OF CORRECTIONS AND REHABILITATION FACILITIES.

REQUESTING THE HAWAII CORRECTIONAL SYSTEM OVERSIGHT COMMISSION TO ESTABLISH AN ADVISORY COMMITTEE TO DEVELOP RECOMMENDATIONS ON THE IMPLEMENTATION OF ALTERNATIVE MODELS FOR REHABILITATION AND RESTORATIVE JUSTICE ON OʻAHU.
REQUESTING THE PLANNING DEPARTMENT OF EACH COUNTY TO ESTABLISH KUPUNA-FRIENDLY BUILDING PERMIT REQUIREMENTS FOR PARKING ACCESSIBILITY AND PRIVATE BUSINESSES OPERATING HOURS.

REQUESTING THE CITY AND COUNTY OF HONOLULU TO CONSIDER CHANGING THE CONFIGURATION OF BICYCLE LANES AND ON-STREET PARKING STALLS TO ALIGN WITH THE FLOW OF VEHICULAR TRAFFIC, ESPECIALLY ON ONE-WAY STREETS.
URGING THE COUNTIES TO INTEGRATE THE SAFE SYSTEM APPROACH INTO ROAD AND TRANSPORTATION DESIGN, ESPECIALLY WHEN REDUCING OR ELIMINATING OFF-STREET PARKING REQUIREMENTS, TO INCREASE PEDESTRIAN SAFETY.

REQUESTING THE DEPARTMENT OF HAWAIIAN HOME LANDS AND STATEWIDE OFFICE ON HOMELESSNESS AND HOUSING SOLUTIONS TO DEVELOP A COORDINATED SUPPORT AND STABILIZATION PATHWAY FOR NATIVE HAWAIIAN BENEFICIARIES EXPERIENCING HOMELESSNESS OR EXTREMELY LOW INCOME.
ENDORSING WAIKIKI AS A WORLD SURFING RESERVE.

REQUESTING THE UNITED STATES CONGRESS TO PASS LEGISLATION TO AMEND THE CIVIL RIGHTS ACT OF 1964 TO PROHIBIT DISCRIMINATION ON THE BASIS OF SEX, SEXUAL ORIENTATION, AND GENDER IDENTITY IN EMPLOYMENT, HOUSING, PUBLIC ACCOMMODATIONS, EDUCATION, FEDERALLY FUNDED PROGRAMS, CREDIT, AND JURY SERVICE.

REQUESTING THE HAWAII STATE ENERGY OFFICE TO CONVENE A WORKING GROUP TO STUDY THE POTENTIAL IMPACTS OF LARGE DATA CENTERS ON HAWAII'S ELECTRIC UTILITIES, RATEPAYERS, NATURAL RESOURCES, AND CLIMATE GOALS.
REQUESTING THE PUBLIC UTILITIES COMMISSION TO PROVIDE A REPORT TO THE LEGISLATURE ON THE PROGRESS OF THE HAWAII ELECTRIC RELIABILITY ADMINISTRATOR.

REQUESTING THE DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH TO ESTABLISH A WORKING GROUP TO STUDY ACCESSIBILITY BARRIERS FOR MULTI-FAMILY HOUSING NOT COVERED BY THE FEDERAL FAIR HOUSING ACT AND GOVERNED BY CONDOMINIUM ASSOCIATIONS AND PLANNED COMMUNITY ASSOCIATIONS.
CONVENING A WORKING GROUP TO ESTABLISH A NONPROFIT ORGANIZATION RECOGNIZED BY THE STATE TO SUPPORT ARTS AND CULTURE ENGAGEMENT AND RELATED INITIATIVES.
CONVENING A WORKING GROUP TO ESTABLISH A NONPROFIT ORGANIZATION RECOGNIZED BY THE STATE TO SUPPORT SANCTUARIES AND OTHER CONSERVATION-RELATED INITIATIVES FOR ENDANGERED AND OTHER SPECIES.

URGING THE DEPARTMENT OF EDUCATION, IN COORDINATION WITH THE BOARD OF EDUCATION, TO DEVELOP A PLAN TO TRANSITION THE SCHOOL BUSES USED FOR PUBLIC TRANSPORTATION TO ELECTRIC BUSES TO EXPAND THE BENEFITS ALREADY DEMONSTRATED IN OTHER PLACES.

REQUESTING THE DEPARTMENT OF LAND AND NATURAL RESOURCES AND DEPARTMENT OF EDUCATION TO COLLABORATE TO ESTABLISH A FORMAL, LONG-TERM COLLABORATIVE PROGRAM TO EXPAND, EQUITABLY DISTRIBUTE, AND SUSTAIN TREE-CANOPY COVERAGE ACROSS PUBLIC SCHOOLS STATE WIDE.

URGING THE DIVISION OF STATE PARKS OF THE DEPARTMENT OF LAND AND NATURAL RESOURCES TO CONVENE A TASK FORCE TO IMPROVE STATE PARKS, AND TO DEVELOP APPROPRIATE BRANDING AND NARRATIVES FOR PARKS, LANDMARKS, AND OTHER SIGNIFICANT PLACES THROUGHOUT THE STATE.

URGING APPROPRIATE AUTHORITIES TO REDEVELOP THE PALI LANES PROPERTY TO PRESERVE ITS HISTORIC MID-CENTURY ARCHITECTURE AND PROVIDE FOR MEANINGFUL RECREATIONAL, CULTURAL, AND COMMUNITY-SERVING USES THAT BENEFIT THE RESIDENTS OF KAILUA AND WINDWARD OAHU.
URGING THE DEPARTMENT OF EDUCATION TO PROVIDE INFORMATION TO STUDENTS ON HOW TO PREREGISTER TO VOTE BEFORE REACHING VOTING AGE.

categories.name: Food & Nutrition
categories.description: School meals, SNAP, local food and sugary drinks.

categories.name: Tobacco, Vaping & Alcohol
categories.description: Keeping tobacco and vaping from kids, and alcohol policy that puts health first.

categories.name: Health Care & Rights
categories.description: Getting care, paying for it, and the rights that come with it.

categories.name: Family & Economic Security
categories.description: Wages, leave, rent and the tax credits families live on.

categories.name: Getting Around Safely
categories.description: Crossing the street, catching the bus, getting to school.

categories.name: Climate & Environment
categories.description: Pesticides, heat, wildfire and clean water.

issues.name: Free school meals for every student
issues.description: Free breakfast and lunch for every public school student, with a free-lunch pilot as a first step.

issues.name: Free school meals for more families
issues.description: Free school breakfast and lunch for more students from low-income families, charter schools included.

issues.name: Lower school meal prices
issues.description: Cut what families pay for school meals, down to a quarter of what the meals cost to make.

issues.name: No child denied a meal over unpaid bills
issues.description: No student is turned away from a school meal, or singled out, because of meal debt.

issues.name: More local food in school meals
issues.description: Help schools buy and serve food grown in Hawaiʻi, and keep farm to school programs running.

issues.name: Farm to Families food program
issues.description: A state program that gets food from local farms to families who need it.

issues.name: Make SNAP easier to get and keep
issues.description: Simpler rules, longer renewals for kūpuna, and a working sign-up system for SNAP food benefits.

issues.name: More SNAP help for more families
issues.description: Raise the income limit for SNAP and restore food benefits to their 2023 levels.

issues.name: Replace food aid lost in the shutdown
issues.description: State money to cover the food assistance spent during the 2025 federal government shutdown.

issues.name: SNAP nutrition education
issues.description: Keep funding the statewide nutrition classes that come with SNAP.

issues.name: SNAP match for healthy local food
issues.description: Match SNAP dollars spent on healthy food grown in Hawaiʻi.

issues.name: SNAP sign-up before prison release
issues.description: Let people apply for SNAP before they leave prison, and ease the ban for past drug convictions.

issues.name: No surge pricing on SNAP and WIC foods
issues.description: Stop stores from raising prices on the fly for groceries people buy with SNAP or WIC.

issues.name: No SNAP for sugary drinks and candy
issues.description: A proposal to stop SNAP from paying for sugary drinks and candy.

issues.name: No tax on groceries
issues.description: Take the general excise tax off groceries, starting with food bought with SNAP or WIC.

issues.name: A fee on sugary drinks
issues.description: A small fee on each sugary drink sold, with the money going to health programs.

issues.name: Warning labels on sugary drinks
issues.description: Health warning labels on drinks with a lot of added sugar.

issues.name: Let counties regulate tobacco sales
issues.description: Let each county pass its own, stronger rules on selling tobacco and e-cigarettes.

issues.name: Flavored tobacco sales ban
issues.description: End the sale of flavored tobacco and nicotine products, including flavored vapes.

issues.name: Disposable vape ban
issues.description: End the sale of disposable e-cigarettes in Hawaiʻi.

issues.name: FDA proof required to sell vapes
issues.description: Only vapes with federal FDA approval can be sold here, certified every year by the maker.

issues.name: State directory of approved vape makers
issues.description: A state list of e-cigarette makers that certify they follow federal rules.

issues.name: Higher tobacco and vape taxes
issues.description: Raise taxes on cigarettes, little cigars and vapes, with more of the money going to health.

issues.name: Limit nicotine levels in products
issues.description: Set a safe limit on nicotine and stop the sale of products above it.

issues.name: Phase out tobacco sales by birth year
issues.description: Never sell tobacco or e-cigarettes to anyone born after January 1, 2005.

issues.name: Seizure of untaxed tobacco products
issues.description: Treat untaxed tobacco products as contraband, the same as untaxed cigarettes.

issues.name: Cigars shipped by mail
issues.description: Proposals to let large cigars and pipe tobacco be shipped straight to people's homes.

issues.name: Lower the DUI limit to .05
issues.description: Lower the legal blood alcohol limit for driving from .08 to .05.

issues.name: Tougher consequences for drunk driving
issues.description: Longer license loss for repeat drunk driving, and child support from drivers who kill a parent.

issues.name: Higher liquor taxes
issues.description: Raise the liquor tax and tie it to alcohol content and inflation; HIPHI opposes bills that cut it.

issues.name: Looser alcohol sales rules
issues.description: Proposals to ship beer and spirits to homes, grow brewpubs and redefine draft beer.

issues.name: Cancer warnings on alcohol ads
issues.description: Every alcohol ad carries a warning about cancer risk.

issues.name: Youth substance misuse prevention funds
issues.description: Fund campaigns and community groups that prevent and treat youth substance misuse.

issues.name: Legal adult-use cannabis
issues.description: Proposals to legalize, tax and regulate cannabis for adults.

issues.name: Single-payer health care for Hawaiʻi
issues.description: One public health plan, Hawaii Care, covering everyone who lives in the state.

issues.name: State program to forgive medical debt
issues.description: The state buys up medical debt and forgives it.

issues.name: Protect preventive care and vaccines
issues.description: Keep children's preventive care and vaccines covered under trusted medical guidelines.

issues.name: End non-medical vaccine exemptions
issues.description: School vaccine exemptions only for medical reasons; HIPHI opposes bills that widen them.

issues.name: State buys vaccines for providers
issues.description: The state buys vaccines and gives them free to health care providers.

issues.name: Youth mental health app pilot
issues.description: A one-year pilot of a mental health app for young people in Hawaiʻi.

issues.name: Protect gender-affirming care
issues.description: Protect patients and providers of gender-affirming care, and stop insurers from denying it.

issues.name: Update sex marker on birth certificates
issues.description: Let people change the sex listed on their Hawaiʻi birth certificate.

issues.name: Protect abortion and birth control
issues.description: Protect abortion and birth control in the state constitution and keep medication on hand.

issues.name: Safety for immigrant families
issues.description: Limits on immigration enforcement at schools, clinics and in police custody.

issues.name: No prices based on your personal data
issues.description: Stop companies from setting prices using data they collect about you.

issues.name: Hygienists can place temporary fillings
issues.description: Let dental hygienists place temporary fillings in community health settings.

issues.name: Rural community health worker pilot
issues.description: Community health workers in rural areas who connect people with care.

issues.name: Tax credit for training health students
issues.description: A bigger tax credit for health workers who train students, open to more kinds of providers.

issues.name: Workers’ comp for new grads in training
issues.description: Workers' compensation for recent high school graduates in summer work programs.

issues.name: Licenses for Canadian dental grads
issues.description: A proposal to license graduates of Canadian dental schools for community service in Hawaiʻi.

issues.name: Paid family and medical leave
issues.description: Paid time off to care for a new child, a sick family member or yourself.

issues.name: A higher minimum wage
issues.description: Reach an $18 minimum wage sooner and pay tipped workers the full wage; HIPHI opposes bills to slow it.

issues.name: Bigger child and dependent care credit
issues.description: A bigger tax credit for the cost of child and dependent care.

issues.name: Bigger tax credit for low-income renters
issues.description: A bigger renters' tax credit that more low-income households can get.

issues.name: Cash support for families with babies
issues.description: Direct cash payments to households with very young children.

issues.name: Tax credit for family caregivers
issues.description: A tax credit for people who care for a family member without pay.

issues.name: 3% yearly cap on rent increases
issues.description: Limit rent increases to 3% a year, and none in a tenant's first year.

issues.name: Pilot to keep homes for local residents
issues.description: A county pilot that pays homeowners to keep homes for local residents.

issues.name: Higher taxes on top earners
issues.description: Higher income tax rates for the highest earners.

issues.name: Tax capital gains fairly
issues.description: Tax profits from selling stocks and property more like regular income.

issues.name: Tax real estate investment trusts
issues.description: End the tax break that lets real estate investment trusts avoid state income tax.

issues.name: Graduated tax on property sales
issues.description: A higher tax rate on the most expensive property sales.

issues.name: Income tax changes and tax credit caps
issues.description: Changes to income tax rates and brackets, with limits on some tax credits.

issues.name: Funding for community nonprofits
issues.description: State grants for community groups that meet unmet social service needs.

issues.name: Poverty alone is not child neglect
issues.description: Being poor alone does not count as child abuse or neglect.

issues.name: No tax on period products
issues.description: Take the general excise tax off pads, tampons and other period products.

issues.name: Legal sports betting
issues.description: Proposals to legalize and tax sports betting in Hawaiʻi.

issues.name: Free bus rides for kids
issues.description: Free bus rides and school bus passes for keiki, starting with pilots on some islands.

issues.name: Free public transit statewide
issues.description: Fare-free buses in every county, paid for by a higher tax on petroleum products.

issues.name: Fund Safe Routes to School
issues.description: Steady money for safe walking and biking routes to school, from small fees on cars and deliveries.

issues.name: More red-light and school speed cameras
issues.description: More red-light cameras and speed cameras in school zones.

issues.name: Fairer jaywalking rules
issues.description: Let people cross mid-block when it is safe, and cap jaywalking fines at $25.

issues.name: Drivers stop for people in crosswalks
issues.description: Drivers stop and wait until people in the crosswalk are safely across.

issues.name: Let people cross during the countdown
issues.description: Let people start crossing while the countdown timer is running.

issues.name: Pedestrian safety pilot program
issues.description: A three-year pedestrian safety pilot in the smaller counties.

issues.name: Safer pedestrian signals at crossings
issues.description: Head-start walk signals and accessible crossing signals at state intersections.

issues.name: Safer walking routes next to schools
issues.description: Safety improvements for people walking next to schools.

issues.name: Summer Streets car-free road pilot
issues.description: Each county closes some roads to cars for walking, biking and community events.

issues.name: Funding for Maui wildfire health study
issues.description: Keep funding the study that tracks the health of people exposed to the Maui wildfires.

issues.name: Funding to fight invasive species
issues.description: Fund the work to stop invasive species and protect native lands from fire.

issues.name: Protect students from extreme heat
issues.description: Heat safety rules for student athletes, and a plan for keeping students safe outdoors.

issues.name: Plan for a changing climate
issues.description: A statewide plan and a university center to help Hawaiʻi adapt to climate change.

issues.name: Wildfire hazard map and brush clearing
issues.description: Map wildfire risk statewide and clear brush near roads and power lines.

issues.name: Ban on neonicotinoid pesticides
issues.description: End the sale and use of neonicotinoid pesticides, with few exceptions.

issues.name: Ban the pesticide Telone by 2030
issues.description: End use of the pesticide 1,3-dichloropropene, sold as Telone, by 2030.

issues.name: Better public reporting of pesticide use
issues.description: Report where and when restricted pesticides are used, every three months and online.

issues.name: Pesticide-free buffer zones
issues.description: No restricted pesticide spraying within half a mile of schools, parks and elder care homes.

issues.name: Clearer rules for water shortages
issues.description: Clearer rules for when the state can declare a water shortage or emergency.

issues.name: Replace cesspools with cleaner systems
issues.description: Loans to help homeowners replace cesspools, and tests of new wastewater systems.

issues.name: Study for packaging recycling program
issues.description: Study packaging waste to design a program where makers pay for recycling.

issues.name: Right to a clean environment amendment
issues.description: Put the right to clean air, clean water and a healthy climate in the state constitution.
